confirmed.title: Scheduled-spike hazard term is mis-specified: exp(−Σ w_k·P_k) is not (1−P_k) survival, and it violates the resolved⇒~100 boundary requirement
confirmed.argument: The unified formula adds spikes as Dirac masses w_k·δ(t−t_k)·P_k inside λ(t), so P_arrival = 1 − exp(−∫λ) makes each spike contribute a survival factor exp(−w_k·P_k). But for a scheduled event with per-occasion success probability P_k, the correct survival factor is (1 − P_k). These diverge badly exactly where it matters: with w_k=1 and P_k=0.7 the formula gives survival exp(−0.7)=0.497 instead of 0.30; with P_k=1 (event certain at the scheduled date) it gives P_arrival = 1−e^{−1} ≈ 0.632 instead of 1.0 — directly violating the user's accepted requirement that resolved/certain events read ~0/~100. No fitted w_k can fix this globally because −ln(1−P_k)/P_k is not constant in P_k. Separately, δ-functions inside an intensity that is also multiplied by exp(γ·M(t)) (does the spike get modulated? is M evaluated at t_k⁻ or t_k⁺?) leaves the integral ambiguous as written.
confirmed.fix: Model survival multiplicatively: S(t,T) = exp(−∫_t^{T_eff} λ_bg(u)·e^{γM(u)} du) · Π_{t_k ∈ (t,T_eff]} (1 − P_k), i.e. each spike contributes hazard mass −ln(1−P_k) rather than P_k. This is exact for Bernoulli occasions, makes P_k=1 give P_arrival=1, keeps the diffuse integral well-defined (no δ inside the exp(γM) modulation), and reduces to the plan's form only in the small-P_k limit. Update the design doc (stage A) before the fitting script (stage B) encodes the wrong likelihood.
confirmed.verifier_note: The math is verified correct: a Dirac spike w_k·P_k·δ(t−t_k) inside λ contributes hazard mass w_k·P_k, giving survival exp(−w_k·P_k) instead of the exact Bernoulli survival (1−P_k). At P_k=0.7 that's 0.497 vs 0.30; at P_k=1 arrival caps at 1−e^{−1}=0.632 instead of 1. The correction factor −ln(1−P_k)/P_k varies from ~1 to ∞ across P_k, so no fitted constant w_k repairs it, and the plan explicitly prices P_k off state variables (Fed futures) that routinely sit at 0.8–0.95 — the exact regime of worst divergence. The defect is not acknowledged in §5 Open Questions, and stage B would encode the wrong likelihood into the Polymarket fits. The proposed fix (multiplicative Π(1−P_k) survival, spikes outside the integral) is the standard exact treatment. Two overreaches in the finding, neither refuting: (1) the "resolved ⇒ ~0/~100" requirement is enforced by the separate settlement pin (shipped, 97/3) and impossibility pin, not by the spike term — the real breakage is pre-event pricing of a certain scheduled occurrence at 63% — so the boundary-violation headline is overstated; (2) the δ-modulation ambiguity is a misreading: as written the spike sum is additive outside exp(γM), unambiguously unmodulated. Severity: major, not blocker — the error is confirmed and must be fixed in the stage-A design doc, but it is a localized one-line respecification with a known exact replacement, changes no architecture/staging/validation/kill-criterion, and the plan's own shadow-run + per-horizon calibration KPIs would catch the miscalibration before production.

confirmed.title: The Polymarket 'faster-than-fixed-λ decay' does not evidence Gamma-prior λ-learning: it is confounded by NO-resolution selection, live news flow, and longshot-bias unwinding
confirmed.argument: The plan's sole empirical support for 'silence learns the rate' is that NO-resolved deadline markets decay faster than the constant-λ glide. Three alternative explanations each independently produce the same observation: (1) Selection/conditioning — a calibrated market price is a martingale; averaging only over trajectories that resolved NO mechanically selects paths where YES-negative information arrived, so the conditional path decays faster than the unconditional survival curve under ANY correct model, including fixed-λ with heterogeneous priors. The pilot fit uses exactly this conditioning (13 of 27 trajectories are NO-resolved). (2) The exemplar market was not news-silent: 'US x Iran ceasefire by Mar 31' during Dec 2025–Mar 2026 sat in a heavy news cycle, and its observed path drops 0.645→0.245 in the first lifetime quartile (~7 days) — a news-shock profile, not a smooth silence glide. (3) The plan itself documents 10–30% longshot bias on long-dated NO tranches that unwinds toward expiry; that unwind is observationally identical to super-exponential decay and will be absorbed into the fitted 'silence-strength', biasing it upward. Fitting λ-learning on these slopes as staged will bake in a systematically too-aggressive silence decay.
confirmed.fix: Change the fitting protocol in stage B: (a) fit silence decay only on trajectory segments verified quiet in daatan's own news-indexer (forecast_match / article counts as a covariate — the data exists), not on raw NO-resolved price slopes; (b) include YES-resolved markets' pre-arrival segments so the estimate isn't outcome-conditioned; (c) de-bias longshot premium first via a per-horizon calibration curve (price→outcome frequency) fit on all 110 markets, then fit hazard dynamics on calibrated probabilities. Treat raw market decay as an upper bound on the silence effect, and make the Gamma-prior strength a parameter the daatan shadow-run (stage D) can falsify per horizon bucket.
confirmed.verifier_note: All data claims verified against pm_hist.json: 13 of 27 trajectories NO-resolved; ceasefire quartiles 0.645/0.245/0.155/0.075 vs fixed-λ glide 0.540/0.404/0.228 (matches plan's cited numbers); first-quartile daily deltas (−0.11, −0.11, −0.08, +0.09) show a news-shock profile, not a silence glide, and the sibling regime-fall market confirms an active news window. The martingale-conditioning argument is mathematically correct: E[P_t | NO] = E[P_t(1−P_t)]/(1−P_0) decays with information-driven variance growth under any calibrated model, so NO-conditioned decay faster than the unconditional glide does not evidence λ-learning-from-silence. The plan's §2 cites this comparison as the sole empirical support, §3 step 1 fits λ-learning on raw decay slopes with no silence-identification mechanism, and §3's own longshot-bias anchor (10–30% unwind) is a third confounder absorbed into the fit. Not acknowledged in Open Questions. Refutation attempts failed: downstream guardrails (validation on own forecasts, shadow run, kill criterion) mitigate but compare against a weak frozen-estimate baseline that a miscalibrated aggressive decay could still beat. Severity major rather than blocker: the Gamma-prior mechanism is independently motivated, the flaw is confined to the offline stage-B fitting protocol (zero prod risk), and the proposed fix (news-indexer quiet-segment covariate, YES pre-arrival segments, longshot de-biasing) is concrete and cheap — but as staged the fit would bake in an upward-biased silence-strength, so it must be corrected before stage B runs.

confirmed.title: 'Clock as one extra pseudo-source in the logit pool' double-counts news, applies recency decay twice, and cannot deliver the promised deadline glide to ~0
confirmed.argument: Stage C injects P_clock(t) as one more member of pool_sources. Three math problems. (1) Double-counting: M(t) is computed from the same article stances that already sit in the pool, so each article moves P twice — once directly as a pool member, once through exp(γ·M) inside the clock member; γ fitted offline (where articles enter only via M) will be mis-calibrated in a pool where they also vote directly. (2) Units/decay mismatch: the pool already applies recency_weight with a 7-day half-life to each article (forecaster.py L749–754, config recency_half_life_days=7.0), and M(t) applies its own e^{−(t−t_i)/τ} kernel — two independent decays on the same evidence, so effective evidence half-life is roughly halved and the fitted τ is wrong in situ. Also, a stance is 'P(event by deadline)' in the pool but 'hazard elevation' in M — the same number with two incompatible semantics. (3) Boundary failure: pool_sources computes a weighted MEAN of logits, which is bounded between its members; with logit_clamp=0.01 the clock member contributes at most logit(0.01)=−4.6, and old articles never vanish (recency_floor=0.02), so at a quietly-passed deadline the pooled P converges to ~0 only if w_clock/Σw → 1 — a weight schedule the plan never specifies. As written, 'deadline reached quietly → the glide reaches ~0 on its own' (plan §Boundaries) is not a property of the proposed stage-C architecture.
confirmed.fix: Pick one composition and specify it in stage A: either (preferred) the hazard engine OWNS temporal forecasts — articles enter only through M(t), the pool is bypassed, and settlement override sits on top; or, if the pseudo-source bridge is kept for stage C, (a) the clock member's λ must be the UN-modulated prior hazard (no M(t)) so news isn't counted twice, (b) give it an explicit weight schedule w_clock(t) → dominance as t → T_eff (e.g. w_clock ∝ 1/time-remaining, verified to hit ≤3% at deadline given clamp and floor), and (c) disable the pool's recency decay for evidence that also feeds any M(t). Add a unit test: stale 0.8-stance articles + quiet passed deadline must output ≤0.03.
confirmed.verifier_note: Verified against the code: pool_sources (aggregation.py L144) is a convex combination of member logits, so pooled P is bounded by its members; with logit_clamp=0.01 (config.py L54) the clock member contributes at most logit ≈ −4.6, and recency_floor=0.02 (config.py L51) keeps stale bullish articles voting forever — so the §Boundaries promise that "the glide reaches ~0 on its own" at a quiet deadline holds only if w_clock dominates the pool, and the plan specifies no clock weight or schedule at all. The double-decay claim is also correct: forecaster.py L749–758 applies a 7-day-half-life recency factor to each article's pool weight while the plan's M(t) applies its own e^{−(t−t_i)/τ} kernel to the same articles, so offline-fitted τ/γ (fit on a composition where articles enter only via M) are miscalibrated in situ. The double-counting claim holds at minimum as a fatal underspecification: the only λ the plan defines is news-modulated (exp(γ·M(t))), Stage C keeps articles voting directly in "the existing logit pool", and the plan never says the pseudo-source uses the un-modulated hazard. None of this appears in §5 Open Questions (which cover market data, UI explainability, archetype mix). Refutation attempts fail: Stage C is the only stage shipping runtime behavior and is what Stage D's shadow-run/kill-criterion evaluates, so the composition flaw corrupts the decision the plan hinges on; the impossibility pin (bullet 2) rescues only the terminal instant, not the separately-promised glide; the config flag is on/off, not a weight schedule. Severity: major, not blocker — the hard pins bound the worst user-visible outcome (wrong glide ending in a discontinuous snap rather than a permanently wrong number), and the fix is a specification change within the plan's own stated end-state (§2 "articles stop voting on P"), but as written Stage C double-counts evidence, invalidates the offline parameter fits, and cannot deliver a stated user requirement.

confirmed.title: γ, m₀, and the kernel τ are not identifiable from Polymarket price data — the stage-B fit can only pin λ₀, and the plan's fit/validate split double-uses daatan data
confirmed.argument: γ and m₀ govern how OUR extractor's article stances modulate λ; Polymarket trajectories contain prices only — no article stream, no stances, no evidence-mass series — so no likelihood written on pm_hist.json has any gradient in γ or m₀. Similarly, 'fit the relaxation constant τ on post-event bleed-back' fits the market's mean-reversion time constant (an equilibrium of trader behavior), which is not the same object as the decay kernel of our stance evidence; transplanting it is an unargued identification-by-analogy. The only data that jointly observes (stances, time, outcomes) is daatan's own context_snapshots history — which the plan reserves for validation (step 2) and shadow comparison (step 3). As staged, either γ/m₀/τ ship hand-tuned (contradicting 'fitted, not argued') or they get fit on the validation set, invalidating the kill criterion.
confirmed.fix: Re-scope stage B honestly: PM data fits λ₀ per topic class, the horizon calibration curve, and (with the corrected protocol from the silence finding) bounds on silence-strength. Fit γ, m₀, τ on daatan's own resolved forecasts (context_snapshots stance/weight series + outcomes) with a temporal train/test split (e.g. resolved-before/after a cutoff date), keeping the shadow-run period strictly out-of-sample for the kill criterion. State expected sample size first — if daatan has too few resolved temporal forecasts to fit 3 parameters, say so and default γ, m₀ to conservative priors with the shadow-run as the fit set for the NEXT iteration, not this one.
confirmed.verifier_note: Verified against the plan text and pilot data. pm_hist.json contains only {t,p} price points plus outcome metadata (checked programmatically across all 27 trajectories); the plan's M(t) definition requires per-article (w_i, s_i, t_i) streams from our extractor, so γ (which enters only via exp(γ·M)) and m₀ (only via M's denominator) have zero gradient in any PM-price likelihood — non-identifiability confirmed. Plan §3 promises all five parameters "fitted, not argued," but step 1 (the only step with named fit data) fits only τ/λ-learning/λ₀ from PM, and step 2 reserves the sole dataset that jointly observes stances+time+outcomes (daatan context_snapshots) for validation — so γ/m₀ are either hand-tuned or double-use the validation set. The τ critique also holds: PM post-event bleed-back measures market price mean-reversion (shock relevance decay + offsetting news + longshot bias), a different object from the decay kernel of our stance evidence; the plan transplants it without argument. Not acknowledged in §5 Open Questions. One overstatement: the kill criterion (step 4) rides on the prospective shadow run, which remains a valid out-of-sample test even if step-2 data is used for fitting (only step 2's validation claim is compromised), provided parameters freeze before the shadow period — which the plan never states. This narrows but does not refute the finding: stage B as designed cannot deliver 3 of the 5 parameters it promises to fit, contradicting a core stated principle and requiring a re-scope of the fitting data plan before stage B is built. Major, not blocker: workable fixes exist (fit γ/m₀/τ on daatan resolved forecasts with a temporal split, or ship conservative priors with the shadow run as next-iteration fit data), and the prospective shadow run still provides a legitimate kill test.

confirmed.title: M(t) does not 'relax to 0 with time constant τ': the ratio kernel plateaus at the consensus stance for ~τ·ln(Σw/m₀), re-creating the frozen-estimate failure for well-covered events
confirmed.argument: For a burst of agreeing evidence with total weight W and common stance s, M(t) = s·W·e^{−t/τ}/(m₀ + W·e^{−t/τ}). While W·e^{−t/τ} ≫ m₀, M ≈ s — flat, no relaxation. Decay only begins once the decayed mass falls to ~m₀, i.e. after a delay of τ·ln(W/m₀); with W/m₀ = 100 that is ~4.6τ of plateau before any relaxation. Consequences: (1) the plan's stated semantics ('relaxing to 0 with time constant τ') are wrong, and heavily-covered events — exactly the Knicks-class cases motivating the redesign — keep λ pinned at e^{γs} long after the news stops; (2) any τ fit against bleed-back curves under the assumption of exponential relaxation will be confounded by the unmodeled mass dependence (fitted τ varies with coverage volume, not just topic). Note the observed PM bleed-back the plan cites (~3–4 weeks) is the plateau+decay composite, not τ itself.
confirmed.fix: Decide the intended behavior explicitly in the design doc. If mass-dependent persistence is desired, keep the form but (a) correct the stated semantics, (b) parameterize the fit as plateau-then-decay so τ and m₀ are separately identified from bleed-back shape, and (c) cap Σw_i (e.g. saturating transform) so 30 syndicated articles can't buy months of plateau. If pure τ-relaxation is desired, decay M itself toward 0 — M(t) = M̂·e^{−(t−t_last)/τ} where M̂ is the mass-shrunk snapshot at the last evidence time — which restores the advertised semantics.
confirmed.verifier_note: The algebra is verified correct: for a single evidence burst of weight W and stance s, M(t) = sWe^{−t/τ}/(m₀+We^{−t/τ}) plateaus at ≈s until t ≈ τ·ln(W/m₀), contradicting the plan's stated semantics (§2, "relaxing to 0 with time constant τ"). Refutation attempts fail: (1) the clock term and silence-learning keep P moving, so "frozen" is overstated (it is a persistent e^{γs} bias, not a freeze), but the semantics defect stands; (2) although m₀ is listed among fitted parameters, §3 step 1 explicitly fits τ from bleed-back timescale, and the Polymarket price data has no observable W analog, so the plateau length τ·ln(W/m₀) is unidentified — the fitting confound is real; (3) config.py's max_articles=10 doesn't bound the design's accumulating temporal kernel, and even W≈5, m₀=0.5 gives a ~2.3τ plateau (the finding's W=50/4.6τ example is inflated ~10x given decisiveness_floor=0.5 ≈ one article, but this only weakens the illustration); (4) the formula drives Stage A (design doc) and Stage B (parameter fitting), so it is material. Not acknowledged in §5 Open Questions. Not a blocker because the approach survives and the fixes (honest semantics or decaying M directly, plateau-aware fit parameterization, mass cap) are cheap and local, but it mischaracterizes the core formula in the motivating well-covered case and would corrupt the Stage B fit — major.

confirmed.title: The hazard model's P(t) is a function of calendar time, but no production recompute mechanism is staged — the clock ships but never ticks
confirmed.argument: Every temporal property the model promises (silence decay, deadline glide, impossibility pin at deadline−τ_lead, survival drift-up for negative claims) requires P to be re-evaluated as t advances with no new articles. Production updates are exclusively push-driven: news-indexer matcher → daatan POST → Oracle, further throttled by the matcher's per-forecast push cooldown; the daatan cron directory contains backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health — no per-forecast recompute (the plan itself notes this in §1 and §6). Stages A–D add the clock term and a shadow-run daily driver, but the production path that would evaluate P(t) daily — and the ≥80%-crossing Telegram alert in context.ts, which fires only on snapshot writes — is never staged. The 77-of-102 stale-forecast problem, the #1 diagnosed failure, therefore survives a full A–D rollout: the published number remains a stale sample of a now-correct curve, and boundary pins fire only if an unrelated article happens to arrive after the deadline.
confirmed.fix: Add an explicit stage (before or with C) for the production time-driver: a daily daatan cron that iterates open temporal forecasts and either calls a cheap Oracle 'reprice from cached evidence + clock' endpoint (no search/LLM — pure formula evaluation, so cost is negligible) or evaluates the survival curve locally from stored per-forecast parameters, then writes a snapshot (which also arms the existing 80% alert path). The shadow-run driver from stage D can be this same job in shadow mode — build it once, dual-purpose, and note that the forecast cache (cache_ttl_seconds=3600 keyed on question) must not serve stale P(t) across days.
confirmed.verifier_note: The finding is grounded and survives refutation. Plan §1 itself diagnoses "NO mechanism that recomputes an estimate on a quiet day" as the top failure (77/102 stale forecasts), yet stages A–D (§4) contain no production time-driver: A=doc, B=offline fitting, C=clock term inside the Oracle logit pool (only evaluated on push-driven Oracle calls), D=shadow-run ending at "decide". Verified: /home/mark/projects/daatan/daatan/src/app/api/cron/ has six routes, none recompute forecasts; context.ts fires the 80%-crossing Telegram alert only inside snapshot-write paths (lines 138/183/263) reached from the push endpoint; matcher.py L142–164 gates even article-driven pushes with a per-forecast cooldown. §5 Open Questions does not acknowledge this gap (it lists market data, UI explainability, archetype mix), and §6's "no per-forecast recompute cron exists" is a reviewer note, not a planned resolution. Refutation attempts fail: promotion of the stage-D shadow driver to production is never stated, and the production wiring (host repo, snapshot writes, alert arming, cheap reprice endpoint) is non-trivial and unstaged. Consequence as claimed: after full A–D, silence decay, deadline glide, survival drift-up, and the impossibility pin never manifest in published numbers, and the boundary alert only fires if an unrelated article arrives. Minor nit: the proposed fix's cache caveat is overcautious for a once-daily driver (forecast cache TTL is 3600s per config.py L105–107), though clock-dependent P indeed must not be question-keyed cached. Severity: major, not blocker — the design math is sound and stage D builds most of the mechanism; the omission is fixable with one explicit stage, but as written the plan does not ship the remedy for its own #1 problem and the gap is unacknowledged.

confirmed.title: Parameters are fitted to market prices, not outcomes — the model inherits documented market miscalibration
confirmed.argument: Plan §3 step 1 fits τ on 'post-event bleed-back' and λ-learning on 'silent-period decay slopes' — both are regressions onto Polymarket price trajectories. Prices are not probabilities: the plan's own anchors section admits long-dated NO tranches carried 10–30% mid-life longshot bias, and the pilot's single largest market (pm_markets.json record #1, 2024 Presidential Election, $1.53B) is the market with documented whale manipulation; prices also embed fees and risk premia. Fitting decay slopes to these prices bakes the market's longshot bias into λ₀ and the silence-strength parameter by construction, then the plan proposes to 'check calibration per horizon bucket' — against the same biased target.
confirmed.fix: Fit λ₀/τ/silence-strength by maximum likelihood on outcome data — event arrival times and censoring times across all scraped markets (a survival-likelihood fit) — not on price paths. Use market prices only as a diagnostic comparator (does our hazard curve beat the market's Brier?), or explicitly debias prices (e.g., fit a monotone recalibration map price→outcome frequency on the resolved set) before using them as targets.
confirmed.verifier_note: Core claim verified against the plan and pilot data: §3 step 1 (lines 107-111) fits τ, λ-learning, and λ₀ to Polymarket price trajectories, and the plan's own anchors (lines 119-124) admit 10-30% horizon-growing longshot bias in those prices. Because the bias varies over market life, it distorts silent-period decay slopes, not just levels — fitted silence-strength will be systematically too weak and λ₀ too high, inheriting the market's miscalibration by construction. The proposed fix (survival-likelihood MLE on the 110 resolved markets' arrival/censoring times, prices as diagnostic only) is feasible with data already in hand, and nothing in §5 Open Questions acknowledges the issue. However, two parts of the finding are misreadings that reduce severity from blocker: (1) the plan does NOT validate against the same biased target — §3 steps 2-3 validate on daatan's own resolved forecasts and score the shadow-run by Brier/log score per horizon bucket against realized outcomes, with an explicit kill criterion in step 4, so a bias-contaminated fit cannot silently reach production; (2) the $1.53B election-market/whale point is weak — pm_hist.json's 27 decay trajectories are the Iran/ceasefire deadline ladders, not the election market, so the manipulated market does not sit in the decay-slope fit set; τ is additionally a timescale fit largely insensitive to level bias. Net: a real, unacknowledged methodological flaw in stage B whose worst realistic outcome is a wasted fitting stage or a sound architecture wrongly failing its kill gate — major, not blocker.

confirmed.title: Silence-decay evidence and fit are conditioned on NO-resolution — survivorship bias overstates how informative silence is
confirmed.argument: The Bayesian-hazard section's empirical support is 'Polymarket NO-resolved deadline markets decay faster than fixed-λ predicts (ceasefire 0.65→0.24→0.15→0.07)', and step 1 fits λ-learning on 'silent-period decay slopes' of those markets. Conditioning on NO-resolution removes exactly the paths where quiet periods ended in a jump to YES (the plan's own Khamenei example: 0.34→0.05 then +0.93 in a day). The calibrated quantity is E[outcome | quiet k days] over ALL markets, and a NO-conditioned fit will make silence pull P down too aggressively — the model will underprice quiet-then-arrive events, which is the worst failure mode for a platform scoring user reputation on these numbers.
confirmed.fix: Fit the silence-learning parameter on the unconditional sample: for every deadline market, use its full quiet-exposure record with the outcome as arrival-time or right-censoring in the negative-binomial/Gamma survival likelihood. Then validate with the unconditional check: bucket all markets by quiet-streak length and compare model P against realized outcome frequency in each bucket.
confirmed.verifier_note: Finding verified against the plan and data: (1) plan lines 59–61 base the silence-decay claim solely on NO-resolved markets; (2) line 111 fits λ-learning on 'silent-period decay slopes' with no censoring/arrival treatment, which is only well-defined for NO trajectories; (3) pm_hist.json confirmed 14/27 trajectories are YES-resolved, so the conditioned fit discards the half of the sample containing quiet-then-arrive paths; (4) the plan's own Khamenei anchor (0.34→0.05 quiet decay then +0.93 jump) is an in-sample instance of the failure mode. Refutation attempts failed: step 1's generic 'resolved' wording doesn't cure the NO-conditioned evidence and undefined YES-slope treatment; the kill criterion (aggregate Brier per horizon bucket) is dominated by majority-NO outcomes, so over-aggressive decay can improve mean Brier while underpricing quiet-then-YES tails; the 'can't time arrivals' acknowledgment addresses jump prediction, not fit-sample bias; not listed in Open Questions. Severity major rather than blocker: the hazard mechanism itself is sound and the fix (unconditional censored-survival likelihood + quiet-streak-bucketed calibration check) is a contained change to the offline stage-B fitting script caught at design stage, not a premise-level rejection of the architecture.

confirmed.title: Kill criterion can't fail and can't be decided: the baseline is the frozen oracle and the buckets are too thin
confirmed.argument: The kill criterion compares against 'current behavior' — a push-only oracle with no recompute cron (confirmed: daatan src/app/api/cron/ has no per-forecast recompute route) that holds stale numbers past deadlines. Any model with a deterministic glide-to-boundary wins every NO-resolved deadline case mechanically, so the fitted λ machinery (γ, m₀, τ, Bayesian silence-learning) is never actually tested — a two-line 'linear decay to deadline + existing pins' patch would beat the baseline just as hard. Simultaneously, 'beat per horizon bucket' on Daatan's own resolved set (order tens of forecasts total, single digits per bucket) cannot reach significance in any bucket, so a strict per-bucket reading is undecidable and a loose reading is auto-pass. As written, stage D's gate cannot produce a 'kill' verdict for the interesting component.
confirmed.fix: Split the comparison: baseline B0 = current pooling; baseline B1 = current pooling + trivial deterministic clock (linear or fixed-λ decay to deadline + shipped settlement/impossibility pins). Ship stage C only if the fitted model beats B1, not just B0, on paired per-forecast score deltas (bootstrap CI on the pooled paired difference, pre-registered minimum effect); demote per-horizon-bucket Brier to a diagnostic view. This also reorders the build: B1 is a one-day patch that captures most of the user-visible win while the fitting work proceeds.
confirmed.verifier_note:
The finding's factual premises all check out against the plan and code, and no refutation holds.

Premise 1 — the baseline is frozen: confirmed. The cron directory (/home/mark/projects/daatan/daatan/src/app/api/cron/) contains only backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health — nothing recomputes a per-forecast estimate; the plan itself concedes this twice (lines 12-13: "there is NO mechanism that recomputes an estimate on a quiet day"; line 153: "no per-forecast recompute cron exists"). The only shipped time-independent correction is the settlement pin in forecaster.py (lines 885-908), which requires ≥settlement_min_sources articles — it does nothing on quiet deadlines. So on every NO-resolved deadline forecast the baseline scores its stale frozen number at resolution (plan line 14: 77/102 open forecasts stale 7+ days). Any monotone glide-to-boundary — including a two-line linear decay — mechanically beats that on exactly the case class the plan targets. The reviewer's phrase "maximal by construction" is slightly overstated (a forecast frozen on the correct side scores fine), but the directional point stands: the comparison in lines 116-117 tests "clock vs no clock", not the fitted machinery (γ, m₀, τ, Gamma-prior silence learning, p_det) the plan spends stage B building. No B1-style trivial-clock baseline appears anywhere in the plan.

Premise 2 — buckets too thin: confirmed. The kill criterion is item 4 of section 3, keyed to the item-3 shadow-run KPIs ("Brier/log score per horizon bucket"), and "current behavior" only exists for daatan's own forecasts — the Polymarket set (110 markets / 27 trajectories, verified in pm_markets.json/pm_hist.json) has no live-Oracle counterpart, so it cannot serve this comparison. With 102 open forecasts, the subset resolving during a shadow window, split across horizon buckets, is single digits per bucket; a strict per-bucket win requirement is undecidable and a loose one auto-passes. The plan specifies no sample-size floor, no pairing, no effect-size threshold, and no tie-breaking rule.

Refutation attempts that fail: (a) "per horizon bucket" cannot be read as referring to the PM calibration checks — those are fitting-stage diagnostics with no Daatan baseline to beat; (b) reading the gate as merely a "don't ship something worse" guard doesn't rescue it — the plan's stated purpose (line 116-117: "keep the simple one") is precisely to decide whether the complex model earns its keep, and a gate that any decay function passes cannot make that decision; (c) this is not acknowledged in section 5's Open Questions, which cover market-data identity, UI explainability, and archetype mix — not evaluation design.

Severity: major, matching the claim. It does not invalidate the temporal-model design itself or block stages A-C, but it makes the plan's only decision gate (stage D) incapable of answering the question the plan poses, risking either shipping unjustified complexity or an undecidable verdict. The proposed fix (add B1 = pooling + trivial clock + shipped pins as the bar to beat, pooled paired score deltas with a bootstrap CI, buckets demoted to diagnostics) is a contained amendment to section 3 and also correctly observes that B1 alone captures most of the user-visible staleness win — a genuine build-order insight.

confirmed.title: Pilot sample cannot support the parameter count or the transfer claim: ~10 effective events, one topic, one volume stratum
confirmed.argument: The fit targets λ₀ per topic class, τ, γ, m₀, and silence-strength, but the pilot is 27 trajectories from ~19 event families of which 13 are a single correlated Iran cluster; all markets come from tag_slug=politics with minimum volume $24.5M. Three transfer problems a skeptic can verify: (a) effective independent n ≈ 10, far below what per-topic λ₀ plus four shared parameters needs; (b) Daatan's portfolio includes sports (the motivating Knicks case), statutory-process, and threshold claims — none represented, so 'λ₀ per topic class' has no data for most of Daatan's classes; (c) $24M+ markets have saturated news coverage (p_det≈1), so silence-strength fitted there is an upper bound — precisely the parameter that must transfer to Daatan's thin-coverage forecasts where silence is least informative.
confirmed.fix: Before fitting: expand the scrape across tags (sports, crypto/econ, science) and down the volume distribution; validate with grouped cross-validation holding out whole event families (never split tranches of one event across train/test); fit hierarchically with shrinkage to a global prior; and declare the PM fit as a prior to be re-fit on Daatan's own accumulating resolved set, with the shadow run logging the data needed for that re-fit from day one.
confirmed.verifier_note: Data verified directly: pm_markets.json has 110 markets, min/median vol $24.6M/$55.6M, sourced solely from tag_slug=politics (plan line 158); pm_hist.json has 27 trajectories of which exactly 13 are one correlated Iran-conflict cluster, and the rest collapse to ~10-14 independent event families (Ukraine and 2024-US-election keys are internally correlated). All three factual claims in the finding check out. Refutation attempts fail: (1) the plan does say the pilot precedes a larger bulk scrape (line 107-109), which softens the raw n≈10 arithmetic, but the planned full scrape is still politics-only deadline-ladder markets, so 'λ₀ per topic class' (line 105) has one topic class of data and the volume/p_det saturation critique applies to the full scrape too; (2) the p_det gating (lines 63-68) structurally discounts silence for thin-coverage forecasts but the silence-strength parameter is still fitted only in the p_det≈1 regime and the gating form is asserted, not fitted — partial mitigation only; (3) the shadow run + kill criterion (steps 2-4) prevent a bad fit from shipping but convert a cheap pre-fit fix into a likely stage-D failure and possible false kill of the approach; validation on Daatan's resolved set is validation, not the re-fit-as-prior the fix proposes. Aggravating: the plan's own empirical justifications for the Bayesian-hazard design (lines 59-61) and its 'known empirical anchors' (lines 119-124) are drawn from inside the correlated Iran/election clusters. The Open Questions section does not acknowledge fit-data coverage, CV methodology, or transfer, so no acknowledged-discount applies. Severity: major, not blocker — stage B is offline with zero prod risk and the kill criterion guards shipping; the exposure is wasted stages B-D and a false negative on the approach, and the fixes (multi-tag scrape, volume stratification, grouped family-level CV, hierarchical shrinkage, PM-fit-as-prior with day-one shadow logging for re-fit) are cheap and pre-fit.

confirmed.title: Shadow-run KPIs don't test the new component: time-to-repricing is identical by construction, and resolution-only scoring rewards the mechanical glide
confirmed.argument: Both live and shadow models consume the same push-driven article stream (matcher.py pushes once per match; settlement pin already ships in the live oracle at forecaster.py:885-900), so 'time-to-repricing from settlement-grade news to boundary snap' is the same number for both models — it measures news-indexer/pipeline latency, not the temporal model, yet the plan lists it as a first-class comparison KPI. Meanwhile scoring Brier only per horizon bucket at resolution over-rewards any model that glides to the boundary late in life regardless of mid-life calibration, and the shadow run must wait months for Daatan's long-dated forecasts to resolve before yielding a verdict.
confirmed.fix: Reclassify time-to-repricing as a pipeline SLO monitored independently of the model comparison. For the model gate, score both models at sampled evaluation times across each forecast's life (time-averaged Brier or CRPS against the eventual outcome), not just at resolution. To avoid waiting months, add a replay backtest: rerun both models over daatan's stored context_snapshots/forecast_match history for already-resolved forecasts, which exercises the clock on real quiet gaps with known outcomes before the live shadow run starts.
confirmed.verifier_note: Two of the three sub-claims are misreadings of the plan. (1) "Resolution-only scoring rewards the mechanical glide" is contradicted by plan lines 113-114 and 122-123: the shadow run computes P(t) daily and scores Brier/log per horizon bucket, with the pilot anchor explicitly requiring per-horizon calibration checks because long-dated markets were miscalibrated mid-life — that IS time-sampled scoring across the forecast's life, which penalizes late-glide-only models in long-horizon buckets. (2) "Must wait months for a verdict" ignores plan step 2 (line 112), which is exactly the reviewer's proposed replay backtest — validation on daatan's own resolved forecasts via context_snapshots history + outcomes — run before the shadow phase, plus step 1's fit on ~hundreds of resolved Polymarket trajectories. (3) The time-to-repricing point does survive: the settlement override is shared and already live (forecaster.py:885-910, retro PR #230), both models consume the same matcher push stream, so "minutes from settlement-grade news to boundary snap" measures pipeline latency, not the temporal model (and a daily-cadence shadow could even look spuriously slower). However, the plan's kill criterion (line 116) gates on per-horizon-bucket score, not time-to-repricing, so the mislabeled KPI cannot corrupt the model decision. What remains is a real but cosmetic labeling defect fixable by one line (reclassify as pipeline SLO), not the claimed major flaw in the validation design.

confirmed.title: KPI set omits calibration curves, sharpness, and CI coverage — the model's CI output is never validated
confirmed.argument: The plan's own anchor says 'calibration must be checked per horizon bucket' but the only proposed scores are bucketed Brier/log score. Bucketed Brier with single-digit-n buckets is noise, and a model hedged toward base rate can win it while being useless for the product (which needs decisive numbers near boundaries). Separately, the model emits confidence intervals as a first-class output (aggregation.py widen_ci_for_thin_evidence, and the plan's degradation ladder keys UX behavior off 'wide CI'), yet no KPI checks whether stated CIs cover realized outcomes — an uncalibrated CI silently corrupts the 'insufficient evidence' ladder and the 80%-crossing Telegram alert threshold.
confirmed.fix: Add to stage D: reliability diagrams with bootstrap bands (pooled, plus per-horizon as diagnostic), Brier decomposition into calibration and resolution (report sharpness explicitly), and empirical CI coverage (fraction of resolved outcomes falling inside the stated band, target ≈ nominal). Pre-register these alongside the paired-score gate so the decision isn't made on bucketed Brier alone.
confirmed.verifier_note: The finding is accurate on every load-bearing claim. Plan lines 113–117 list only bucketed Brier/log score and time-to-repricing as KPIs, and the kill criterion is pre-registered on bucketed Brier alone, while the plan's own empirical anchor (line 123) explicitly states "calibration must be checked per horizon bucket" — bucketed Brier conflates calibration with resolution and is noisy at small per-bucket n, so the anchor is unmet. The CI is a genuine first-class shipped output (pool_sources returns ci_low/ci_high; widen_ci_for_thin_evidence at aggregation.py:162–193 inflates it as a confidence self-report; daatan persists aiCiLow/aiCiHigh in context.ts) and no proposed KPI validates empirical coverage. The gap is NOT acknowledged in the plan's Open Questions (section 5 covers market data, UI explainability, archetypes only). Two framing errors in the finding — the degradation ladder is keyed off evidence state with CI width as output rather than input, and the 80% Telegram alert consumes the point estimate, not the CI — weaken the "corrupts the ladder/alert" phrasing but do not touch the core defect. Severity minor: the shadow-run design already collects the data needed; the fix is extending stage D's KPI list (reliability diagrams, Brier decomposition, CI coverage) before the decision gate — cheap, non-architectural, but worth pre-registering so the ship/kill call isn't made on noisy bucketed Brier alone.

confirmed.title: No component recomputes quiet forecasts — the plan's central failure mode has no assigned owner, driver, or cost budget
confirmed.argument: The plan's #1 diagnosed failure is 'updates are 100% push-driven... NO mechanism recomputes an estimate on a quiet day', and every temporal feature (silence decay, deadline glide, impossibility pin) only manifests if something re-evaluates P on a clock. But the staged implementation (Section 4, stages A–D) never names the component that does this. Verified: /home/mark/projects/daatan/daatan/src/app/api/cron/ contains only backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health — no per-forecast recompute; the only scheduled forecast-touching job is external-market-sync.yml (hourly, external markets only). Retro is a stateless request/response API with a 90s per-call budget (config.py forecast_timeout_seconds) whose full pipeline runs search + 2 LLM calls per article; naively re-running run_forecast() daily for ~100 open forecasts is ~100 pipeline runs/day of LLM+search cost and does not even exercise the clock term correctly (a quiet day returns the same articles). Stage D ('shadow-run... compute the new P(t) daily for all open forecasts') silently depends on this nonexistent driver.
confirmed.fix: Make the requote driver an explicit Stage C deliverable with an owner: a cheap retro endpoint (e.g. POST /requote) that reprices P from persisted model state (λ posterior, deadline, direction) + clock with NO search and NO LLM calls, plus a daily daatan cron route (src/app/api/cron/requote) triggered by a GitHub Actions schedule like external-market-sync.yml that iterates open forecasts. Budget it: 100 forecasts × one arithmetic call/day ≈ free; full pipeline reruns reserved for the existing push path.
confirmed.verifier_note: Verified against the plan and code: (1) src/app/api/cron/ contains only backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health — no per-forecast recompute; the only scheduled forecast-touching job is external-market-sync.yml (hourly, external markets only). (2) Plan §1 names 'NO mechanism recomputes an estimate on a quiet day' as the top failure, §2 asserts 'the glide reaches ~0 on its own', and §3.3/Stage D require computing P(t) daily — yet no stage in §4 delivers the component that evaluates P on a clock. Stage C's clock pseudo-source only changes what the push-triggered pipeline computes, not when it runs. (3) The gap is not in §5 Open Questions; the §6 parenthetical '(note: no per-forecast recompute cron exists)' is a diagnosis restated for reviewers, not a deliverable or owner. (4) Retro is stateless (config.py forecast_timeout_seconds=90; forecaster.py runs full search + per-article LLM per call) and persists no λ posterior, so the proposed cheap requote requires an unmade architectural decision about where temporal model state lives — strengthening the finding. One sub-claim in the finding is wrong: a naive daily full-pipeline rerun WOULD exercise the clock term (the clock/silence terms are functions of evaluation time, not of which articles return), so the objection is cost and statelessness rather than correctness — but that does not refute the core. As written, the plan does not deliver the mechanism that its own #1 diagnosed failure and every temporal feature (silence decay, deadline glide, impossibility pin) depend on, and closing the gap involves a real design decision (state persistence for cheap repricing vs. expensive full reruns), so this must be resolved before the plan is approved.

confirmed.title: Per-claim metadata has no home: retro is stateless, the Prisma schema has no fields for it, and no repo is assigned the migration or the reclassification write path
confirmed.argument: Section 2 requires per-claim state — archetype (+secondary), direction, claim_deadline, τ_lead, state_variable, p_det prior — created once at forecast creation and MUTATED later by reclassification signals ('election scheduled for Sep 11' updates the spike date). But: (a) retro has no database (config.py: a data_dir with leaderboard.json; ForecastRequest carries only question + optional articles), so the Oracle cannot look this metadata up; (b) daatan's Prediction model (prisma/schema.prisma:257+) has claimText/resolveByDatetime/confidence/aiCiLow/aiCiHigh but no column for any of the new fields; (c) p_det is defined off news-indexer's forecast_match history, which lives in a third repo's Postgres that neither daatan nor retro reads; (d) the reclassification channel does not exist — the matcher pushes articles to daatan's /context, daatan calls the Oracle, and nothing in that loop can write back 'the spike date moved' to wherever metadata lives. The plan assigns none of this, and it is the largest schema/API-contract change in the whole project.
confirmed.fix: Decide and write into the plan: daatan owns the metadata (Prisma migration: a ClaimMeta json column or table on Prediction), runs the creation-time classifier, and passes the metadata in every /forecast request body (retro stays stateless). p_det: have news-indexer include its match-rate stats in an existing surface daatan already receives (the push payload or a small endpoint), or derive it from daatan's own ContextSnapshot history. Reclassification: extractor emits an optional 'schedule_signal' field; daatan applies it to ClaimMeta on push. Add all three contracts to Stage C's task list explicitly.
confirmed.verifier_note: Every leg of the finding verifies: retro/api config.py + models.py ForecastRequest confirm the Oracle is stateless with no field for the §2 metadata; daatan prisma/schema.prisma Prediction has no column for archetype/direction/claim_deadline/τ_lead/state_variable/p_det; p_det is defined off news-indexer's ForecastMatch table in a third repo's Postgres that neither daatan nor retro reads; the push loop (matcher.py → route.ts:95-99 → Oracle with claimText+articles only) has no write-back path for the plan's stated 'Claims MIGRATE' reclassification signals. The plan's §4 Stage C says 'claim classifier at creation' without assigning storage, request contract, p_det source, or reclassification channel, and §5 Open Questions does not acknowledge any of it (it lists market data, UI explainability, archetype mix). Refutation attempts fail: 'recompute classifier per request' contradicts the plan's own 'at forecast creation, one cheap call' plus mutation semantics; 'derive p_det from daatan ContextSnapshots' is a fix the plan doesn't contain, not a counter-argument; Stage A is described as capturing this plan, not deciding new contracts. The plan's central engine is parameterized by state with no home across three repos — the largest implied schema/API change and wholly unassigned — so Stage C cannot be scoped or built as written.

confirmed.title: Stage C's 'clock as one extra pseudo-source in the logit pool' cannot satisfy the accepted boundary requirements — especially with zero articles, where the pipeline returns insufficient_data before pooling even runs
confirmed.argument: Two concrete failures. (1) Zero-article path: the impossibility pin is specified as 'pin ~0/100 exactly, zero articles needed', but run_forecast returns _empty_response(insufficient_data=True) when search finds nothing (forecaster.py:608-642) or when no stances survive (forecaster.py:799-857) — pooling, and therefore any pool-member clock term, is never reached. Daatan then NULLS the estimate on insufficientData (context.ts:120-122), so an impossible claim with no coverage reads 'Insufficient evidence', violating the user's accepted resolved⇒~0/~100 requirement. (2) Bounded pooling: logit pooling is bounded by its members (the documented reason the settlement override exists — forecaster.py:885-891 'pooling is bounded by its most confident member'); a clock pseudo-source at finite weight can never drive the pool to ~0/100 against surviving article stances, whose weights are floored (recency_floor=0.02, config.py:51) and never vanish. The deadline glide 'reaches ~0 on its own' only if the clock weight grows unboundedly — at which point it is not a pool member, it is an override.
confirmed.fix: Split the clock into two mechanisms in Stage C: (a) a mid-life tilt that may live in the pool (fine as a weighted pseudo-source), and (b) boundary pins implemented as explicit post-pool overrides alongside the settlement override, with stated precedence (settlement > impossibility/deadline pin > pool), evaluated even on the zero-article/insufficient-data path — i.e. the temporal engine must run before the empty-response short-circuit, using the per-claim metadata rather than articles.
confirmed.verifier_note: Both claimed failures verify against the code. (1) forecaster.py returns _empty_response at 608-642 (no search results) and 799-857 (no usable stances) before Step 4 pooling ever runs, so a clock implemented as a pool member is unreachable on the zero-article path; daatan's context.ts then nulls confidence/aiCiLow/aiCiHigh on insufficientData, meaning the plan's own impossibility example ("no article will ever say so", §1) would read "Insufficient evidence" instead of the §2-required ~0/100 pin "zero articles needed". (2) pool_sources (aggregation.py:117-158) is a convex combination of member logits, strictly interior whenever any contrary member has positive weight; article weights are floored (recency_floor=0.02) so a finite-weight clock cannot drive the pool to the boundary — the settlement override comment at forecaster.py:885-891 documents exactly this bounding limitation, so Stage C's mechanism contradicts the rationale of the override the plan itself cites as shipped. Refutation attempts fail: the plan never specifies running the temporal engine before the short-circuits; Stage C is the only implementation stage (D is shadow/decide); and §2 Boundaries is an accepted user requirement not listed in §5 Open Questions. The plan as written specifies a mechanism structurally incapable of its own hard requirement and of the §3 time-to-repricing KPI; the fix is a design change that must land before implementation.

confirmed.title: Daily requotes routed through the existing snapshot writers will spam the ContextSnapshot timeline and fire Telegram 80%-alerts on pure clock drift
confirmed.argument: Every existing write path daatan has (saveNewsIndexerMatch, saveOracleSnapshotOnly, saveContextUpdate in context.ts) creates a ContextSnapshot row, and getContextTimeline renders all of them newest-first on the forecast page — a daily requote of ~100 open forecasts adds ~36k near-identical rows/year and buries real news-driven updates and user context in the timeline UI. Worse, all three paths call notifyIfCrossedHighConfidence (context.ts:28-43,183,263): for survival-direction claims ('X will NOT happen by Dec 31') the plan's clock glide pushes P monotonically UP through 80 with zero new articles, so the nightly requote sends 'high confidence / consider resolving' Telegram alerts whose trigger is silence, not evidence — semantically the alert was built for settlement-grade news (plan §1: 'crosses 80 from below'). The plan's open question about UI explainability acknowledges drift visibility but not the write-amplification or alert-semantics problem.
confirmed.fix: Add to Stage C: the requote path updates Prediction.confidence/aiCiLow/aiCiHigh directly WITHOUT creating a ContextSnapshot (or writes a distinct snapshot kind, e.g. source='clock', excluded from the timeline query and collapsed to at most one visible row per N days), and the 80-crossing alert distinguishes cause — clock-driven crossings either don't alert or send a distinct low-priority 'deadline approaching, silence implies NO' message.
confirmed.verifier_note: The mechanics check out: all three writers in daatan/src/lib/services/context.ts (saveContextUpdate:98, saveNewsIndexerMatch:161, saveOracleSnapshotOnly:242) create a ContextSnapshot and call notifyIfCrossedHighConfidence, getContextTimeline:46 renders all snapshots unfiltered, and no confidence-only write path or recompute cron exists (cron dir: backfill-embeddings/cleanup/external-market-sync/heartbeat/oracle-health/search-health). The finding overstates two things: (1) the crossing guard (context.ts:36) means at most one alert per forecast per crossing, not nightly spam; (2) stages A-D contain no production daily requote — Stage C only adds the clock term to existing push-triggered calls, and Stage D's shadow-run explicitly computes "alongside" without persisting. But it is not refuted: plan §2 promises "deadline reached quietly → the glide reaches ~0/~100 on its own" as user-visible behavior, which requires a periodic requote persisting to Prediction.confidence — a mechanism the plan never designs, and every existing writer it could reuse produces exactly the timeline write-amplification and clock-triggered "consider resolving" alerts described. The alert-semantics half also bites within Stage C alone: one article match on a long-quiet survival forecast pushes P over 80 mostly on clock and fires an alert built (per §1) for settlement-grade news, unactionable before the deadline. The Open Questions entry acknowledges only UI drift explainability, not snapshot volume or alert cause, so the acknowledged-therefore-minor rule applies only partially. Major: the plan's core deliverable lacks a persistence/notification design and the naive implementation degrades two shipped features; the fix (snapshot kind excluded/collapsed in timeline + cause-aware alert) belongs in Stage C.

confirmed.title: retro's forecast cache and response contract assume time-invariant point answers; the plan should return model state instead of a point P, which fixes caching, the requote cost, and the survival-curve contract at once
confirmed.argument: forecast_cache is keyed by (question, max_articles, articles_hash) with TTL 3600 (forecaster.py:461-474, config.py:107), and search_cache holds results 4h — under the plan the correct answer changes with the clock even at fixed inputs, so a cached hit can mask a just-crossed boundary (e.g. T_eff passed 10 minutes ago → still serves pre-pin P for up to an hour), and the in-flight dedup returns one caller's timestamped answer to another. Point-P responses also force every clock tick to be a retro round-trip (feeding finding 1's cost) and make the plan's survival-curve output P(by T) a breaking addition to ForecastResponse that daatan's oracle.ts and news-indexer's matcher.py response parsing (matcher.py:244-266 reads stance/certainty/claim/probability) must all absorb.
confirmed.fix: Specify the API contract in Stage C: the Oracle returns additive optional fields — model state (λ posterior params, claim_deadline, direction, τ_lead, as_of timestamp) and/or the P(by T) grid — alongside the existing mean/std/ci so current consumers are untouched. daatan persists the state and prices P(t) locally in the daily requote cron (no retro call, cache becomes harmless). If a point P must still be served time-sensitively, bucket the cache key by day near boundaries.
confirmed.verifier_note: The finding's core is verified and unaddressed by the plan. (1) Cache: forecaster.py:461-475 keys the forecast cache on (question, max_articles, articles_hash) with cache_ttl_seconds=3600 (config.py:107) and no time component; under the plan's time-dependent P(t), identical inputs no longer produce identical correct outputs, so a cache hit spanning a boundary (T_eff = deadline − τ_lead crossing, plan §2 impossibility pin) serves a stale pre-pin P for up to an hour — directly conflicting with the plan's own §3 first-class KPI of minutes-scale time-to-repricing. The plan never mentions the cache. (2) Requote cost: ls of src/app/api/cron/ confirms no per-forecast recompute mechanism exists; plan §4 Stage C/D never adds a production requote path, and with a point-P contract every clock-driven refresh is a full search+LLM pipeline run — the state-returning contract the reviewer proposes is the architectural decision that determines this cost, and the plan omits it entirely. Not acknowledged in §5 Open Questions. However, two sub-claims are refuted in part: (a) the survival-curve grid is NOT inherently a "breaking addition" — matcher.py:262-265 reads response fields via .get() and oracle.ts types only a subset of the JSON, so additive optional fields break nothing (the reviewer's own proposed fix concedes this); (b) the cache-mask scenario is narrower than argued — daatan's push endpoint (context/route.ts:95-97) always supplies articles, so articles_hash differentiates keys and news-driven settlement updates are never cache-masked; pure-clock staleness only bites a poller, which doesn't yet exist. Despite the overstated sub-claims, the surviving core — Stage C lacks the API contract and cache/requote treatment on which the plan's headline frozen-estimates fix depends — is an architecture-level gap that must be resolved before Stage C is buildable. Severity: major (not blocker: fixes are straightforward — additive state fields, time-bucketed or disabled cache — and don't invalidate the temporal model itself).

confirmed.title: Shadow-run (Stage D) has no defined storage or isolation — writing through existing paths contaminates production UI, Prediction fields, and alerts; retro has nowhere to store it
confirmed.argument: Stage D says 'compute the new P(t) daily for all open forecasts alongside the live Oracle; compare', but every persistence surface that exists writes to production: ContextSnapshot rows appear in the public timeline, Prediction.confidence/aiCiLow/aiCiHigh drive the visible gauge, and both trigger Telegram. Retro itself has no datastore (config.py: flat files under data_dir). The comparison KPIs (Brier per horizon bucket, time-to-repricing in minutes) additionally require timestamped paired series (live P, shadow P, outcome) — minutes-resolution time-to-repricing cannot be reconstructed from once-daily snapshots, so the KPI as stated is unmeasurable with the proposed daily cadence. The kill criterion (§3.4) is only actionable if this data exists.
confirmed.fix: Add a Stage D design line: shadow results go to a dedicated store invisible to prod — simplest is a shadow_estimates table in daatan (predictionId, ts, p, ci, model_version) written by the requote cron with no Prediction update and no notifications, or JSONL on the retro EC2. For time-to-repricing, log the shadow price at every real push event (the news-indexer /context call) in addition to the daily tick, so settlement-reaction latency is measured at event granularity, not daily.
confirmed.verifier_note: Every factual leg of the finding checks out against the code. (1) Plan Stage D is one line with no storage/isolation design. (2) context.ts confirms all estimate write paths (saveContextUpdate, saveNewsIndexerMatch, saveOracleSnapshotOnly) update Prediction.confidence/aiCiLow/aiCiHigh transactionally with the ContextSnapshot insert and all call notifyIfCrossedHighConfidence (Telegram); getContextTimeline exposes every snapshot publicly — there is no non-contaminating persistence surface. (3) The cron dir (backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health) has no recompute mechanism, so the daily shadow tick is new, undesigned infrastructure. (4) retro config.py stores only flat files under data_dir — accurate, though 'nowhere to store' is slightly overstated since JSONL under data_dir is viable (the finding's own fix). (5) The time-to-repricing KPI is stated in minutes while the shadow cadence is daily — internally inconsistent as written; the only partial mitigation (retroactive reconstruction of the deterministic formula at ContextSnapshot timestamps) is itself undesigned and still needs the missing storage. (6) Not in §5 Open Questions, so not 'acknowledged'. The kill criterion (§3.4) — the plan's go/no-go gate — depends on paired timestamped series the plan never arranges to collect. Refutation attempts fail; severity major (not blocker: fixable with a few design lines, no harm until Stage D is implemented, model design itself unaffected).

confirmed.title: Stage C has no recompute trigger, so the clock never ticks and the #1 failure (frozen estimates) is not fixed
confirmed.argument: The plan's own problem statement says updates are 100% push-driven and 77/102 open forecasts were stale 7+ days. Stage C adds the clock as 'one extra pseudo-source in the existing logit pool' — but that pool is only evaluated when news-indexer pushes an article (route.ts calls getOracleForecast only on POST). The daatan cron directory contains no per-forecast recompute (only backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health), which the plan itself notes in §6 — yet no stage builds one. Worse, the impossibility boundary ('pin ~0/100, zero articles needed', §Boundaries) is definitionally untriggerable by pushes. Quiet forecasts stay frozen exactly as today; users see the same two-week-stale 82%.
confirmed.fix: Add an explicit Stage C deliverable: a scheduled recompute sweep over open forecasts (daatan cron route calling the Oracle, or an Oracle-side scheduler that POSTs results back), with a defined cadence (e.g. daily) and idempotence. Make 'the Knicks forecast moves on a quiet day' the stage C acceptance test.
confirmed.verifier_note:
I tried to refute the finding on three grounds and all three fail against the plan text and code.

(1) "The plan already builds a daily sweep" — §3 step 3 does say "Shadow-run: compute the new P(t) daily for all open forecasts alongside the live Oracle", so daily-compute infrastructure is implied. But that is explicitly a shadow computation for KPI comparison in Stage D; no stage deliverable wires any scheduled computation into the live, user-facing estimate. Stage C — the only stage that touches production behavior — puts the clock "as one extra pseudo-source in the existing logit pool", and that pool is evaluated only inside getOracleForecast calls. I verified every getOracleForecast caller in daatan: (a) the news-indexer push handler (src/app/api/news-indexer/context/route.ts:95, POST only), (b) the user-triggered analyze POST in src/app/api/forecasts/[id]/context/route.ts:177, and (c) refreshOracleSnapshot in src/lib/services/oracle-backfill.ts — which is invoked only from the manual admin route src/app/api/admin/forecasts/backfill-oracle-sources/route.ts and deliberately uses saveOracleSnapshotOnly ("WITHOUT touching the user-facing context summary"), so it doesn't move the displayed probability. The cron directory (src/app/api/cron/) contains exactly backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health — no per-forecast recompute, exactly as the plan's own §6 concedes.

(2) "P(t) could be evaluated at read time, so no cron is needed" — plausible architecture (the new P_arrival(t) is an analytic function of t given fixed evidence), but the plan nowhere proposes read-time evaluation; daatan persists probabilities as snapshots (context.ts) and users see the stored number. An unstated alternative mechanism cannot refute an omission.

(3) "It's acknowledged in Open Questions" — §5 mentions UI explainability of "numbers drift without new articles", which presupposes drift happens but never specifies or acknowledges the missing trigger mechanism. So this is not an acknowledged-gap case.

The reviewer is also right that the impossibility boundary (§2 Boundaries: "pin ~0/100 exactly, zero articles needed") is definitionally unreachable by a push-driven pipeline — an event that generates no articles never triggers the code that would pin it. Same for "deadline reached quietly → the glide reaches ~0/100 on its own": nothing evaluates the glide on a quiet day.

Severity: the plan's own §1 names frozen estimates as the primary production failure (77/102 open forecasts stale 7+ days; the Knicks 82% two-week freeze). As staged, Stage C's live behavior still only updates on article pushes, Stage D is shadow/compare/decide with no productionization deliverable, so the plan as written never delivers time-driven updates to users — it fails its own #1 goal. That is a blocker for a design plan, not a polish item. The proposed fix (explicit scheduled recompute deliverable in Stage C with cadence, idempotence, and a quiet-day acceptance test) is well-targeted and cheap, since the Stage D shadow sweep needs the same machinery anyway.

confirmed.title: Settled/impossibility-pinned forecasts stay ACTIVE with no user-visible state and open commitments — a predictable free-points window
confirmed.argument: The `settled` flag is stored only inside the oracleSnapshot JSON and the Telegram alert; there is no Prediction.settled column in schema.prisma and no reference to settled in ForecastDetailClient.tsx or ContextTimeline.tsx. So between settlement pin (97%) and human resolution, a user sees an ordinary ACTIVE forecast at 97% with the commit UI open. Scoring makes this exploitable: rsChange = (0.25 − brier) × 100 with no time discount (prediction-resolution.ts:135), so committing +100 after the pin yields ~+25 RS risk-free, and beats the community peerScore of honest earlier committers. The plan's new impossibility pin (~0 with zero articles) widens this window to every deadline claim — the model literally publishes the answer while commitments remain open. (Earlier committers' aiScore is safe — aiProbabilityAtCommit is snapshotted at commit — the exploit is the late-commit side.)
confirmed.fix: Add to the plan: persist a settled/pinned state on Prediction, render a 'outcome reported — awaiting resolution' banner on the forecast page, and lock (or heavily time-discount) new commitments once the estimate is boundary-pinned by settlement or impossibility. This should ship with or before Stage C's boundary pins.

The plan's §Boundaries generalizes pinning (impossibility pin at ~0/100 with zero articles; deadline glide), making the exploit window systematic for every deadline claim, and neither the plan body nor its Open Questions addresses commitment locking or a user-visible settled state (Open Q #2 is about explaining clock drift, not scoring integrity). One sub-claim is imprecise — the late committer's peerScore vs the converged community is ~0, not better than early committers' — but RS/Glicko/ELO exploitability all hold. Refutation angles fail: the condition pre-exists (settlement pin shipped) but the plan predictably widens it; the plan already claims daatan-side scope; resolution is manual with documented multi-day staleness and no auto-resolve cron. confirmed.title: Clock-driven 80-crossings will spam 'consider resolving' alerts for survival claims weeks before they are resolvable
confirmed.argument: notifyIfCrossedHighConfidence (context.ts:28-43) fires whenever the new estimate crosses 80 from below, settled or not. Under the new model, every survival-direction claim ('X will NOT happen by Dec 31') glides upward through 80 purely on quiet time — by design (§2, P_survival → ~100). Each one triggers a Telegram alert, but the claim cannot actually be resolved until the deadline passes, so the alert is non-actionable noise. The crossing re-arms whenever a contrarian article dips the estimate below 80 and the clock pushes it back over, producing repeat alerts. With ~100 open forecasts and a growing survival portfolio, this degrades the one channel the plan relies on for the resolve-loop.
confirmed.fix: Specify in the plan: the high-confidence alert only fires for article- or settlement-driven moves (use the snapshot `kind` from the explainability fix); add a separate, single-shot 'deadline passed quietly — resolve NO' alert at T_eff, which is the moment human action is actually possible and useful.
confirmed.verifier_note: The finding survives grounding. (a) Code: notifyIfCrossedHighConfidence (daatan/src/lib/services/context.ts:28-43) fires on any 80-crossing from below regardless of cause, and all three write paths (saveContextUpdate, saveNewsIndexerMatch, saveOracleSnapshotOnly) invoke it; the settled flag only annotates, never gates. The code comment (lines 22-27) confirms the re-arm-on-dip behavior the finding cites. (b) Plan math: a survival claim crosses 80 when the remaining hazard integral drops to ln(1/0.8)≈0.22 — for a claim starting near 50%, roughly two-thirds through its window, i.e. weeks-to-months before the deadline; the plan's own pilot anchor (ceasefire NO gliding 0.35→0.93 in survival terms) shows this is the designed common case. (c) Plan text: §1 designates the 80-crossing alert as the 'consider resolving' mechanism; §2 designs systematic pre-deadline crossings for the survival direction; §5 Open Questions covers UI drift explainability but not alert semantics — so the issue is not acknowledged. (d) Shadow-run doesn't refute it: stage C wires the clock pseudo-source into the live logit pool behind a config flag, and every push-triggered recompute flows through the alerting paths; fixing frozen estimates further implies adding a recompute mechanism (no per-forecast cron exists today — verified: cron dir has only backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health). (e) The finding even understates the problem: crossing-based alerting means that when the deadline actually passes (the actionable moment), no alert fires because the estimate is already above 80 — early noise plus silence at T_eff. Independent severity: major — it degrades the single channel the plan relies on for the resolve loop, by design, for an entire claim direction, and the fix is a design decision (gate alerts by move kind; add a single-shot T_eff alert) that belongs in the plan.

confirmed.title: Daily recompute snapshots will drown the user-facing timeline (and the table) in clock ticks
confirmed.argument: The timeline endpoint returns all contextSnapshots ordered desc, and ContextTimeline renders one entry per snapshot. A daily sweep over ~100 open forecasts writes ~36k rows/year of near-identical 'clock tick' snapshots; a 6-month forecast accrues ~180 entries that bury the handful of actual article events users care about. This is a build-order decision (snapshot policy must be designed before the sweep exists), not a style nit.
confirmed.fix: Add a snapshot policy to Stage C: persist a clock snapshot only on material change (e.g. ≥1pt) or at a coarse cadence, and/or render clock drift from the stored curve parameters instead of rows; the timeline UI collapses consecutive clock ticks into one drift segment.
confirmed.verifier_note: The code evidence checks out: getContextTimeline/listContextSnapshots (context.ts:46-58, 186-192) are unbounded, ContextTimeline.tsx maps over every snapshot with no collapsing, no recompute cron exists, and prediction.confidence is a stored scalar (not computed on read) — so fixing the plan's headline "frozen estimates" failure mode does eventually require either periodic writes or render-from-curve, and the plan specifies neither. However, the finding overstates the plan's commitment: Stage C only adds a clock pseudo-source to the existing push-driven path, and Stage D's daily computation is explicitly a shadow-run for KPI comparison with no stated write to the user-facing contextSnapshot table — the "36k rows/year" scenario is a possible naive implementation, not a designed one. Moreover, the plan's formula makes clock drift analytic (P_arrival(t) from fitted parameters; Stage C mandates survival-curve output for a grid of T), so the reviewer's proposed fix is the natural reading. Open Question 2 already acknowledges the adjacent issue (how clock-driven drift is surfaced on the forecast page), though not the snapshot-volume/write-policy question specifically. Net: real but small design gap, partially acknowledged, cheap to close with one sentence in Stage C.

confirmed.title: The survival-curve grid P(by T) has no consumer — sibling-deadline consistency is not a user-visible feature in daatan today
confirmed.argument: Stage C includes 'survival-curve output P(by T) for a grid of T (prices sibling forecasts with different deadlines consistently)', but daatan has no data model linking sibling forecasts and no UI that compares deadline variants; each forecast is priced from its own claim_deadline regardless. As specced, the grid is API surface with no page that renders it and no cross-forecast constraint that consumes it, built inside the riskiest production stage.

confirmed.verifier_note:
Verified against the plan and codebase; the finding survives.

2. The evidence checks out. /home/mark/projects/daatan/daatan/prisma/schema.prisma has no sibling/variant/ladder relation (grep for sibling|variant|ladder|parentForecast finds nothing; only resolveByDatetime per forecast). No cron route recomputes or compares deadline variants (cron dir contains only backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health).

I looked for a refutation in the similar-forecasts machinery and found the opposite. docs/SIMILAR_FORECASTS.md (the active deadline-aware redesign proposal) uses deadline distance as a multiplicative PENALTY (dl_sim gate) — same-event/different-deadline candidates are explicitly scored down in discovery and rejected as dups ("C1 created Jan 1, identical string → not a dup"). daatan's design direction treats deadline siblings as things to separate, not as a ladder to price jointly. The stated rationale is also technically shaky, which weakens any "implicit consumer" defense: siblings are independent forecasts with independent evidence streams and independent λ estimates, so one forecast's P(by T) grid does not actually price another forecast — consistency would require shared-event linkage that doesn't exist.
