Partial mitigation (why not higher severity): the grid is a near-free byproduct — once ∫λ(u)du is computed for the forecast's own deadline, evaluating it at extra T values is a few lines of read-only output and does not touch the flag-gated pooling path, so "riskiest production stage" overstates the exposure. It is scope hygiene (an unjustified deliverable with a false rationale), not a correctness or rollout risk. The proposed fix (name a real consumer or defer to post-shadow-run) is cheap and correct. Independent severity: minor, matching the reviewer's claim.

confirmed.title: Exact ~0/100 impossibility pin is gated on a single unaudited LLM parse (claim_deadline + direction) with no reconciliation or error budget
confirmed.argument: The plan's boundary rule pins a forecast to ~0/100 'exactly, zero articles needed' once deadline−τ_lead passes, and the deadline comes from one cheap LLM call at creation reading claim TEXT, explicitly not resolveByDatetime. The plan's own motivating example (claim says 2025, resolveBy 2027) proves these diverge, but it specifies no divergence-rate measurement, no audit, and no runtime guard. A misparse ('within 90 days of inauguration', a date that names when a report was published, a claim with no date at all) auto-pins a live forecast to 0 — the pin flows through prediction.confidence and, for survival-direction claims gliding up through 80, fires the 'consider resolving' Telegram alert (context.ts:28-43, 183), i.e. it actively prompts the maintainer to resolve on a hallucinated deadline. The same one-shot call also emits direction (arrival|survival); a flipped direction makes the clock drift P the WRONG way — strictly worse than today's freeze. Nothing in the current extractor prompt (extractor.py) parses deadlines today, so there is zero production evidence of this extraction's accuracy. No timezone convention is specified either ('by Dec 31' — UTC? event-local? Polymarket resolves on ET), and the existing forecaster already mixes naive datetime.now() (forecaster.py:711) with UTC elsewhere.
confirmed.fix: Insert a calibration step before stage C: run the classifier over the entire existing portfolio (~102 open + resolved forecasts), measure the claim_deadline-vs-resolveByDatetime divergence distribution and hand-audit all disagreements plus every direction label. At runtime: (a) hard-pin only when BOTH extracted deadline and resolveByDatetime have passed, or when they agree within tolerance; when they diverge, apply only the bounded clock pseudo-source and route a 'deadline disagreement' Telegram alert for one-click human confirmation; (b) store the deadline as an explicit UTC instant with a stated end-of-day convention set at classification time; (c) persist classifier output in the context snapshot so every pin is auditable to its inputs.
confirmed.verifier_note: The finding's factual claims all verify: the plan (§2, lines 81-92) pins P to ~0/100 "exactly, zero articles needed" off a single new LLM extraction (claim_deadline from claim text + direction label) with no reconciliation against resolveByDatetime, no accuracy audit, no timezone convention; extractor.py confirms no deadline field exists today (zero production evidence for this extraction); context.ts:28-43 confirms any confidence write crossing 80 fires the "consider resolving" Telegram alert, so a misparse-driven pin actively prompts human resolution on a hallucinated deadline; forecaster.py:334/711 confirms naive datetime.now() usage. The plan's own mitigations do not cover the failure mode: the degradation-ladder fallback handles only unparseable/failed classification, not confident misparses; the stage-D shadow-run and kill criterion are aggregate KPI gates (Brier per horizon, time-to-repricing) that a few individually catastrophic pins can pass; the §5 Open Questions section does not acknowledge classifier accuracy at all, so the "acknowledged → minor" rule does not apply. However, I downgrade from blocker to major: the pin ships only behind a config flag after a shadow-run with an explicit kill criterion plus validation on daatan's own resolved forecasts (which would catch systematic direction flips); the alert is advisory — a human decides resolution; and the proposed fix (portfolio calibration pass + agree-or-alert runtime rule + UTC convention) is additive to stage C rather than invalidating the design.

confirmed.title: Stage B fits on pilot data whose final price ≠ resolution value and whose histories/metadata are truncated or inconsistent — decay-slope fits learn artifacts
confirmed.argument: Direct inspection of pm_hist.json/pm_markets.json: 'Russia x Ukraine ceasefire by June 30, 2026' resolved YES but its recorded trajectory ends at p=0.07 on 2026-05-08 (7 weeks before the listed end) — to any decay-slope fitter this reads as a textbook NO-glide on a market that actually happened. 'US x Iran ceasefire by April 15' resolved YES, final recorded price 0.18, history ends 2026-04-02 — five days before the event its sibling by-April-7 market confirms. Trump 2024 (the largest-volume market in the set) ends at 0.58 despite YES. 'US strikes Iran by February 28, 2026' carries Gamma end=2026-01-31, contradicting the deadline in its own question text — so using Gamma endDate as the hazard horizon T misaligns the deadline-decay fits the whole model depends on. The plan's headline empirical claim ('NO-resolved deadline markets decay faster than fixed-λ predicts') was computed on this data with lifetime quartiles defined by these possibly-truncated windows; the λ-learning and λ₀-per-topic fits in stage B will inherit every artifact silently. Only 27 of 110 markets have trajectories at all — the attrition mechanism is also uncharacterized (possibly biased toward certain outcomes).
confirmed.fix: Add a mandatory data-prep substage to B: (1) label every trajectory from yes_won, never from last price, and append the resolution value as a terminal point at closedTime; (2) detect truncation (gap between last history timestamp and closedTime > 2 days, or |p_final − resolution| > 0.2) and re-fetch with explicit startTs/endTs pagination or exclude the series from slope fits; (3) parse the deadline from the market question text and reconcile against Gamma endDate, preferring the question-text deadline as T; (4) report the 110→27 attrition cause before trusting topic-level λ₀ fits; (5) re-run the quartile-decay sanity check on the cleaned set before any parameter is adopted.
confirmed.verifier_note: Verified every exhibit against pm_hist.json/pm_markets.json and the pilot scripts. Real: (a) one series (ceasefire-by-Apr-15, YES) has a genuine 6-day terminal gap ending at p=0.185; (b) strikes-by-Feb-28 has Gamma end=2026-01-31 contradicting its own Feb-28 deadline (plus 2 empty endDates), so Gamma endDate is unreliable as hazard horizon T; (c) daily fidelity means YES markets' last recorded price can be far from 1 (Trump 0.58); (d) the plan has no explicit Stage-B data-prep substage. Refuted/overstated: the headline exhibit (ceasefire-by-June-30 'truncated 7 weeks early') is early resolution — history runs to 1 day before closedTime=2026-05-09, a genuine sudden arrival the plan already documents as a phenomenon (Khamenei anchor); the 'label from last price' failure mode is contradicted by the actual code (pm_analyze.py labels won from meta winner; pm_fetch.py stores yes_won/winner/closedTime); the 110→27 'attrition' is a hand-curated 27-question WANT list in pm_hist.py spanning archetypes, not fetch attrition, and the plan says real Stage B bulk-scrapes hundreds; the headline quartile claim (0.65→0.24→0.15→0.07) reproduces exactly on a genuine NO market with near-complete history, so it is not an artifact. Plan-side mitigants: the deadline-from-claim-TEXT principle is already a plan tenet, Stage B is offline, and Stage D validates against daatan's own resolved forecasts with a kill criterion; a T-before-history-end misalignment is visibly broken, not silent. Residual: worth adding a short data-hygiene requirement to Stage B (label from winner, T from question text/closedTime, flag terminal gaps >2d — 3 of 27 series affected). Real gap, but far below blocker; not acknowledged in Open Questions, so it is a genuine minor finding rather than an acknowledged one.

confirmed.title: τ (post-event relaxation constant) is fitted from effectively one independent episode; the plan presents it as a fitted parameter
confirmed.argument: The plan's only named relaxation observation is the Khamenei bump (16→32 then 3-4 week bleed-back). A mechanical bump-then-relax detector over the 27 pilot trajectories finds ~34 candidate episodes, but they are heavily clustered in correlated tranches of the same underlying events (the 4 Iranian-regime tranches all share the Khamenei episode; the Iran-ceasefire tranches share theirs), so the effective independent sample is roughly 10-15 — and in NO-resolved deadline markets the 'relaxation' is confounded with the deadline-decay term itself (the price falls after a bump partly because time is running out, not because the news signal relaxed). Fitting τ — and worse, the plan implies per-topic constants — on this sample yields a number with error bars spanning its plausible range, which then silently controls how long every news bump persists in M(t) for all production forecasts.
confirmed.fix: Make episode mining an explicit deliverable of stage B: define the bump/relax detector, deduplicate episodes across tranches of the same underlying event, restrict to mid-life episodes (far from deadline) or fit τ jointly with the hazard-integral decay, and report the effective N and CI on τ. Precommit a threshold (e.g. ≥20 independent episodes, CI narrower than a factor of ~2); below it, ship τ as a hand-set prior with a documented sensitivity analysis instead of claiming it is 'fitted, not argued', and drop per-topic τ from v1.
confirmed.verifier_note: Verified against pm_hist.json and the plan text. The clustering claim is confirmed: a mechanical bump-then-relax detector finds ~69 raw episodes (reviewer found ~34; threshold-dependent, immaterial) across 27 trajectories, but they collapse to roughly 15-25 independent underlying news shocks — e.g. the May 18/20/23/25 peace-deal bumps appear identically in both peace-deal tranches, the Jan 4-10 Iran bumps in four Iran tranches, and the July-2024 Biden-debate episode in three markets at once. The deadline confound is concretely visible: in NO-resolved deadline markets ('peace deal by May 31', 'US strikes Iran by Jan 31') every detected 'relaxation' bottoms at 0.01 exactly at the deadline — clock decay, not signal relaxation — so the plan's prescribed fit ('fit τ on post-event bleed-back', lines 109-111, one named Khamenei anchor) would bias τ short unless fitted jointly with the hazard-integral decay or restricted to mid-life episodes; the plan specifies neither, nor dedup, nor CI/effective-N reporting. The issue is NOT acknowledged in §5 Open Questions. Two sub-claims are overstated and I discount them: (1) 'effectively one independent episode' — the pilot already has 10-15+ independent shocks and the plan's fit targets a bulk scrape of ~hundreds of tranches; (2) 'the plan implies per-topic τ' is a misreading — line 105 attaches 'per topic class' to λ₀ only. Mitigations exist (validation on own resolved forecasts, shadow-run, kill criterion) but aggregate per-horizon Brier is a blunt instrument for catching one confounded relaxation constant, and τ silently governs how long every news bump persists in M(t) in production. The core finding — the plan's 'fitted, not argued' claim rests on a fitting recipe that is confounded on exactly the data class it names, with no dedup/CI methodology — survives, and the proposed stage-B fix is a genuine plan change, not a nit. Independent severity: major (design-review blocking-worthy change to stage B methodology, but not a blocker since the overall architecture and staged rollout remain sound).

confirmed.title: p_det from per-forecast forecast_match history has a cold-start hole and the match counts are structurally censored downward
confirmed.argument: Every new forecast starts with zero forecast_match rows, so under the plan's ladder it lands in 'no matches ever & p_det≈0 → insufficient evidence, no decay' precisely during the early window where the clock/base-rate output is the whole value proposition — and it is indistinguishable from a genuinely never-newsworthy claim for weeks. Separately, forecast_match systematically undercounts true matchable news flow: matcher.py writes a row only after a successful push (push-first-record-second, lines 210-234), the per-forecast cooldown suppresses all matches inside push_cooldown_minutes (lines 144-166), push_max_forecasts caps fan-out per article, and the similarity-gap filter drops marginal forecasts. A forecast in a busy news cycle can therefore show ~1 row per cooldown window regardless of whether 5 or 50 articles matched — so 'historically matched 5 articles/week' is a measurement of the cooldown, not of newsworthiness, and p_det inherits that bias, muting silence-as-evidence exactly where it is strongest.
confirmed.fix: Two changes to the plan: (1) make the LLM-emitted p_det prior (already in the metadata block) the operative value with hierarchical shrinkage toward a topic-class estimate, only blending in per-forecast history after a minimum exposure (e.g. 3-4 weeks); (2) estimate news-flow intensity from pre-gate match candidates, not ForecastMatch rows — either log candidate matches before the cooldown/dedup gate in matcher.py, or query the article index directly (count embedding neighbors above threshold per week) when computing p_det.
confirmed.verifier_note: Both headline mechanisms are substantially contradicted by the plan and code, but a small residue survives. (1) Cold start: the ladder row the reviewer cites (plan line 100) is a conjunction — "no matches ever & p_det≈0" — and the plan's per-claim metadata (line 85) includes an LLM-emitted p_det prior at creation, inside an explicitly Bayesian section (Gamma prior on λ_bg, posterior updates). A newsworthy new forecast starts with a non-zero p_det prior and lands in "thin/stale news → base rate + clock, wide CI", i.e. it DOES get the clock output; the reviewer's fix (1) acknowledges the prior exists and largely restates the plan's implied design. news-indexer's rematch sweep (rematch.py) also backfills the best in-window article for any forecast with no ForecastMatch rows every sweep, so an on-topic new forecast accrues matches within hours, not weeks. (2) Censoring: push_cooldown_minutes defaults to 5 (config.py:55; .env.example confirms; no infra override found), giving a ~2,016 rows/week ceiling — "~1 row per cooldown window regardless of whether 5 or 50 articles matched" implies a multi-hour cooldown that doesn't exist, and 5 vs 50/week are trivially distinguishable. push_forecast_similarity_gap defaults to 0.0, so the gap filter cited as a suppressor is off by default. push_max_forecasts=5 and record-on-success-only are real but marginal censors (crowded clusters; transient outages retried on next match). Moreover p_det is a saturating gate, and the plan fits silence-strength end-to-end on daatan's own resolved forecasts with a shadow-run kill criterion, so a consistent downward bias in the covariate is largely absorbed by the fitted mapping (fitting and inference share the same censored measurement). What survives: the plan text is internally underspecified — the Bayesian-hazard section says p_det "is estimated per-forecast from its own forecast_match history" and "one that never matched carries none" without stating the prior↔history blending rule or minimum exposure, and ForecastMatch is acknowledged nowhere as a censored proxy (pre-gate candidate counts or index-neighbor counts would be cleaner). That is a design-doc clarification for stage A, not a major hole, and it is not acknowledged in Open Questions — so not refuted, but minor.

confirmed.title: Stage C/D cannot measure or deliver the headline fix: no recompute driver exists, and the shadow-run baseline on quiet days is undefined
confirmed.argument: The #1 diagnosed failure is that estimates freeze because updates are 100% push-driven (77/102 forecasts stale ≥7d). Stage C only adds a clock pseudo-source inside the Oracle call — which still only executes when news-indexer pushes. Listing daatan's cron routes confirms nothing recomputes per-forecast estimates (backfill-embeddings, cleanup, external-market-sync, heartbeat, oracle-health, search-health). So after stage C ships, a quiet forecast still never moves; the deadline glide, silence decay, and quiet-deadline boundary (plan line 92) are all unreachable in production, and stage D's 'compute the new P(t) daily' has no infrastructure. The measurement side is equally undefined: Brier/log-score 'per horizon bucket' against 'current behavior' requires deciding what the current model's estimate IS on days it never updated (carry-forward? skip?), and the validation set — daatan's own context_snapshots — is sparse and event-driven, so naive scoring over snapshot timestamps oversamples news-heavy days and undersamples exactly the quiet periods where the two models differ most. As written, stage D can produce a comparison that shows no difference simply because it only scores on push days.
confirmed.fix: Add an explicit stage between C and D: a scheduled daily recompute driver (daatan cron route or news-indexer job) that re-evaluates every open forecast's estimate — needed by BOTH the shadow-run and the eventual production behavior, so it belongs in the plan as a first-class deliverable, not an implicit assumption. In stage D, precommit the scoring protocol: both models evaluated on the same fixed daily grid, baseline defined as last-value-carried-forward, scores reported per horizon bucket AND per quiet-vs-active day split, so the comparison cannot silently degenerate to push days only.
confirmed.verifier_note: Verified all evidence directly. (1) Push-only is real: the cron directory has only backfill-embeddings/cleanup/external-market-sync/heartbeat/oracle-health/search-health (health pings only); the Oracle is invoked solely from the news-indexer POST handler in src/app/api/news-indexer/context/route.ts, and matcher.py pushes only around a trigger article from a new match. (2) The plan's stages never close the gap: Stage C adds the clock pseudo-source inside the logit pool, which runs only on push, so quiet forecasts still freeze in production — the #1 diagnosed failure (plan lines 10-13) and the line-92 quiet-deadline boundary remain undeliverable; the plan even admits "no per-forecast recompute cron exists" (line 153) but only as a code note, not in Open Questions or as a deliverable. (3) Stage D's kill-criterion comparison validates against context_snapshots, which are written only on push, and no grid/carry-forward/quiet-vs-active protocol is precommitted, so the comparison can degenerate to push days where both models agree. Refutation attempts failed: "compute P(t) daily" implies a shadow-run loop but nothing promotes it into the production estimate path; LVCF is the natural baseline but is unstated and the snapshot-timestamp sampling bias remains. Severity major, not blocker: the fix is an additive plan change (explicit daily recompute stage + precommitted scoring protocol) and stages A-C work is not wasted, but as written the plan cannot ship its headline fix and its decision gate is biasable toward a false null.

confirmed.title: Polymarket bulk scrape has no ToS/rate-limit/reproducibility provisions; fitted constants won't be re-derivable once markets delist
confirmed.argument: Stage B scales the pilot to 'hundreds of political tranches with daily prices' via Gamma + CLOB. The plan asserts 'both public' but never checks Polymarket's Terms of Use or API rate limits, and daatan already treats third-party content conservatively (no full article bodies stored, for copyright). Two concrete risks: (a) unthrottled bulk pagination of prices-history across hundreds of tokenIds is the pattern most likely to get an IP rate-limited or flagged, from a company whose product the model's constants will be derived from; (b) resolved markets age out of default Gamma listings and endpoints change, so if only the fitted constants are kept, λ₀/τ/γ become unreproducible black numbers — no way to re-fit, audit, or extend when the model underperforms in stage D and someone needs to know whether the constants or the model form is at fault.
confirmed.fix: Add three requirements to the stage-B fitting script: (1) review Polymarket's ToS/API terms once and record the conclusion in the design doc; throttle requests with backoff and identify the client via User-Agent; (2) persist the raw scrape (markets + histories + tokenIds + fetch timestamps + script version) as a private S3 snapshot — not in a public repo, mirroring the no-redistribution posture — so every fitted constant is traceable to a frozen dataset; (3) pin fits to the snapshot, never to live API reads, so stage D re-runs are deterministic.
confirmed.verifier_note:
The finding survives in its reproducibility half but its evidence is partly wrong, and the ToS/rate-limit half is largely refuted by the actual pilot code.

What the finding gets factually wrong: the claim "pm_fetch.py/pm_hist.py have no throttling or provenance capture" is contradicted by the scripts themselves. pm_fetch.py line 36 has `time.sleep(1)` between paginated Gamma calls and pm_hist.py line 53 has `time.sleep(1.2)` between CLOB history calls; both send an identifying `user-agent: daatan-research/1.0` header (pm_fetch.py line 4, pm_hist.py line 45). And the raw scrape IS persisted: pm_markets.json keeps all 110 markets including tokenIds (`tok_yes`), and pm_hist.json keeps full per-market metadata plus the complete price history for all 27 trajectories. The rate-limit risk is also overstated on scale grounds: "hundreds of tranches with daily prices" at fidelity=1440 is a few hundred small HTTP requests — minutes of throttled traffic, not a bulk-scrape pattern. The copyright analogy to the news-indexer no-body-storage rule is weak: daily price points are uncopyrightable facts consumed internally for parameter fitting, not redistributed content. The "won't be re-derivable once markets delist" claim is also weakened by the pilot itself, which fetched via `closed=true` — Gamma serves resolved markets, and tokenIds are retained, so re-fetch by ID remains possible unless Polymarket changes endpoints.

What survives: the plan text (§3 step 1, §4 stage B) genuinely contains no reproducibility requirement — nothing says the stage-B fitting script must persist the scraped dataset durably, record fetch timestamps/script version, or pin fits to a frozen snapshot rather than live API reads. The pilot data currently lives only in a session-ephemeral scratchpad directory, so today the 110-market/27-trajectory dataset that motivated the empirical anchors in §3 would vanish with the session. Endpoint/retention changes at Polymarket are outside daatan's control, and stage D's kill-criterion analysis ("are the constants or the model form at fault?") does depend on being able to re-fit against the same frozen data. This is not acknowledged in §5 Open Questions. However, it is a cheap, purely offline requirement (persist the scrape + pin fits to it) on a zero-prod-risk stage, and the natural implementation (the pilot scripts already dump raw JSON) is most of the way there — so it is a documentation/requirements gap, not a design flaw. Independent severity: minor, matching the reviewer's claim, with the ToS/rate-limit portion of the proposed fix mostly already satisfied by the existing script pattern.

confirmed.title: Pilot data cannot support the fitting menu, and fitted parameters are a standing maintenance liability

confirmed.title: Fitting on raw Polymarket long-horizon prices will bake in favorite-longshot bias — the plan reads it as ground truth
confirmed.argument: The plan's central empirical anchor (Section 3) treats Polymarket prices as calibration ground truth and reads 'long-dated NO tranches carried 10-30% mid-life' as evidence that 'longshot bias grows with horizon,' then proposes fitting λ₀/τ/silence-strength to reproduce those trajectories. The prediction-market literature says the opposite of what the plan assumes about direction: the favorite-longshot bias is the single most robust finding in the field, and it WEAKENS as resolution approaches — at long horizons prices are compressed toward 0.50 (longshots systematically OVERPRICED, favorites underpriced), driven by capital constraints and time-discounting, and become nearly unbiased only in the final hours. So the 10-30% mid-life NO prices are not clean signal; they are the market's known long-horizon distortion. Fitting a hazard model to match them teaches the Oracle to reproduce that overpricing, then compounds it because the plan ALSO adds an independent longshot mechanism (wide base-rate bands with no clock decay for scheduled/blind claims). The kill-criterion Brier comparison (step 3) will look fine because the live Oracle is the baseline, not true calibration.

Validate against realized outcomes, not against market mid-prices. Otherwise scope the PM fit to short-horizon segments only, where the market is near-calibrated.

confirmed.title: The unified formula IS an exponential-kernel Hawkes process; conflict-domain evidence says the single τ is likely misspecified
confirmed.argument: λ(t)=λ_bg·exp(γ·M(t)) with M(t) an exponentially-decaying (time-constant τ) kernel-weighted sum of past article stances is, structurally, a self-exciting point process with an exponential memory kernel — i.e. a Hawkes process, which the plan reinvents without naming. This is worth citing/stealing because the Hawkes literature has already answered the plan's open kernel-shape question empirically and by domain: finance/web/social cascades decay fast with an exponential kernel, but conflict and geopolitical events (Daatan's core topic) show much longer memory and are better fit by power-law or per-conflict-type kernels — a single global exponential τ underfits the slow-relaxing geopolitical cases the plan cares about (ceasefire, regime change). The plan already fits λ₀ per topic class but pins one τ and one exponential form.
confirmed.fix: Name it as a Hawkes/self-exciting process in the design doc (part A) so the parameter estimation can reuse standard MLE/EM fitting. In step B fit BOTH an exponential and a power-law kernel per topic class and select by held-out log score; make τ per-topic like λ₀ rather than global.
confirmed.verifier_note: generative lens — not adversarially verified

confirmed.title: The logit-mean pool is not extremized and is fragile to the fat-tailed jumps the plan itself documents — adopt a principled extremizer and/or recency-weighted median
confirmed.argument: The M(t) modulation and the legacy stance pool are weighted MEANS in log-odds space. Two well-established results bear on this. (1) Extremizing: averaging correlated forecasts is underconfident; Satopää's log-odds aggregator applies an extremization factor (α≈2 recommended in Satopää et al. 2014) whose optimal size grows with forecasters' information overlap. Daatan's 'voters' are news articles that heavily share sources and wire copy — extreme overlap — so an un-extremized average is systematically too timid toward 50%, which compounds finding #1. (2) Robustness: the plan notes update distributions are fat-tailed (Biden nomination: 8 daily jumps ≥15pts, line 124) yet aggregates with a mean; Metaculus deliberately uses a recency-weighted MEDIAN precisely because it resists such outliers while staying responsive.
confirmed.fix: Add an extremization step to the log-odds pool with α fit on daatan's own resolved forecasts (step 2 validation), and cap/downweight source-correlated clusters so shared wire copy doesn't count as independent votes. Consider swapping the stance mean for a recency-weighted median to blunt the fat-tailed jumps.
confirmed.verifier_note: generative lens — not adversarially verified

confirmed.title: Halawi et al. 2024 already built and evaluated this exact retrieval-to-aggregation LLM forecaster — steal its IR architecture and its abstention/calibration findings
confirmed.argument: The plan's pipeline (news retrieval → per-article LLM extraction → weighted aggregation) is the same shape as Halawi et al.'s system, which reached near crowd-aggregate on questions published after model cutoff. Two of their findings directly de-risk the plan: (a) their gains came largely from the IR layer — LLM query expansion, relevance ranking, summarization — which is more sophisticated than the plan's relevance² weighting and worth adopting; (b) their system was well-calibrated only when retrieval returned enough relevant articles and they abstained/deferred otherwise — empirical backing for the plan's p_det gate and 'insufficient evidence' rung, and a caution that the LLM stance estimates themselves are underconfident/hedged near certainty, which fights the required resolved⇒~0/~100 boundary and must be corrected by the settlement pin (not by the pool).
confirmed.fix: Cite it in the design doc as prior art and lift its IR stages (query expansion + relevance ranking) into the matcher/extractor rather than relying on relevance² alone. Reuse their calibration/abstention thresholds to set the p_det cutoff empirically. Keep certainty-pinning in the settlement override, not the LLM stance, since LLM stances hedge.

confirmed.title: Conflict-forecasting (ViEWS) evidence confirms the model will predict quiet continuation well but miss onsets — output distributions, not point λ
confirmed.argument: The plan's deliverable framing ('calibrated hazard + fast settlement, not jump prediction', lines 118-124) is validated by the ViEWS literature, which is the closest deployed analogue (monthly geopolitical hazard forecasts up to 3 years out). But that literature adds a sharper lesson the plan should encode: onset prediction is the hard part — onsets are rare and time-varying predictors rarely anticipate them, so these models are strong on continuation/decay and weak on initiation. That is exactly the plan's Khamenei anecdote (0.34→0.05 then +0.93 jump). It means the Bayesian-hazard silence-decay machinery will look good on NO-glide cases and structurally under-warn on surprise onsets, so any Brier evaluation must be stratified by onset-vs-continuation or it will flatter the model. ViEWS-adjacent work also moved to tree ensembles emitting full predictive distributions rather than a point rate.
confirmed.fix: In the shadow-run KPIs (step 3) stratify Brier/log score by onset vs continuation, not just by horizon bucket, so onset misses aren't hidden. Have the engine emit a predictive interval / distribution over P (the plan's thin-evidence CI is a start) rather than committing to point λ.

confirmed.title: Atanasov 'Distilling the Wisdom of Crowds' gives the concrete recipe the plan approximates — decay + skill-weighting + recalibration together, in that combination
confirmed.argument: The plan invents temporal decay (τ kernel) and per-source credibility weighting independently. Atanasov et al. (GJP data, 261 events) showed that the specific combination of temporal decay + differential performance weighting + recalibration is what let statistically-aggregated polls beat prediction markets, and crucially that the biggest edge was at the START of long-duration questions — precisely the long-horizon regime where finding #1 says raw market prices are least trustworthy and where Daatan's frozen/stale-estimate problem bites. This both validates the plan's ingredients and argues they must ship together (a decay kernel without the recalibration layer leaves the extremization/longshot gaps from findings #1 and #3 unaddressed), and it argues for keeping the source-accuracy Ledger (already in the schema per MEMORY) as the performance-weight input.
confirmed.fix: Treat recalibration as a first-class stage in the formula, not an afterthought — fit a recalibration map on daatan's resolved forecasts (step 2) and apply it to the pooled P alongside decay and credibility weighting. Wire the source_accuracy Ledger into the credibility term as the performance weight rather than a static credibility score.

refuted.title: One archetype — diffuse deadline arrival/survival — covers essentially every diagnosed failure; cut spikes and first-passage from v1
refuted.why_refuted:
The finding fails on three grounds.

1. It misreads design framing (section 2) as v1 build scope (section 4). The staged implementation the plan actually commits to is: A) a design doc, B) an offline fitting script, C) "claim classifier at creation + clock as one extra pseudo-source in the existing logit pool, behind a config flag", D) shadow-run with a kill criterion. First-passage pricing and state-variable machinery appear nowhere in stages A–D as build items — they exist only in the unified-formula prose and are explicitly queued behind Open Question 3 ("affects whether threshold/state machinery jumps the queue"). Stage C is, almost verbatim, the reviewer's own proposed fix (deadline glide + impossibility pin + classifier), so "cut it from v1" attacks scope the v1 build does not contain. The degradation ladder already routes unhandled shapes to base-rate+wide-CI or current stance pooling.

2. The one spike-related piece v1 does keep is a correctness guard, not speculative machinery, and cutting it would introduce a regression. The plan's v1 spike handling for claims without a state variable is "holds a base-rate band with wide CI and NO clock decay" — i.e., the classifier's scheduled/diffuse distinction exists to suppress the glide where silence carries no arrival information. A diffuse-only v1 (the proposed fix) would apply silence decay to "Will X win the Sep election" or "Fed cuts 50bps after the March meeting" and glide them toward 0 during the normal pre-event quiet period — a new failure mode worse than the frozen-estimate one being fixed. This is grounded in the pilot data the reviewer did not check: pm_markets.json's 110 markets are heavily scheduled-spike (Fed-meeting tranches, election winners, inaugurations, VP nominations) interleaved with diffuse deadline claims (ceasefire-by-date, TikTok-ban-by-date). The reviewer's ">80% diffuse-deadline" conjecture is empirically false for exactly the claim population the system prices; scheduled claims are not a tail case. Section 1's failure list is deadline-heavy because those are the modes that FROZE — scheduled claims don't freeze visibly, they would be actively mispriced by the proposed diffuse-only glide.

3. The census proposal is subsumed by the plan. Stage C runs the cheap classifier at creation and stage D shadow-runs "the new P(t) daily for all open forecasts" — which requires classifying the entire open portfolio, yielding the archetype census as a byproduct before any engine decision is irreversible (config flag off, kill criterion). Running the census a few days earlier is a sequencing nicety, not a missing safeguard.

Residual truth in the finding — that the threshold/state-variable queue order is unmeasured — is stated in the plan's own Open Questions section (question 3), which the reviewer cites as evidence rather than recognizing as acknowledgment. What remains after removing the misread build scope, the regression-inducing fix, and the already-acknowledged open question is at most a suggestion to run the classifier census as part of stage B instead of C — a scheduling nit, not a major scope defect.

gaps.title: No backfill path: classification runs only 'at forecast creation', so the ~100 existing open forecasts — the plan's own motivating failures — never get temporal metadata
gaps.argument: Section 2 defines per-claim metadata as 'LLM classification at forecast creation, one cheap call', and Stage C ships a 'claim classifier at creation'. Every motivating production case in Section 1 (Knicks frozen at 82%, '77 of 102 open forecasts had no update in 7+ days', the NATO impossibility claim) is an EXISTING open forecast that will never pass through the creation hook. Without archetype/direction/claim_deadline/τ_lead metadata these forecasts fall to the 'unparseable deadline / classifier failure' ladder rung — i.e. current stance pooling — so the shipped system fixes nothing for the current portfolio until it fully churns over months. It also starves Stage D: the shadow run 'for all open forecasts' has no metadata to price the very forecasts it must compare on.
gaps.evidence: Plan Section 2 ('LLM classification at forecast creation'), Section 4 Stage C ('Claim classifier at creation'), Section 1 ('77 of 102 open forecasts', Knicks/NATO cases), Section 3 step 3 ('compute the new P(t) daily for all open forecasts'). No stage mentions retroactive classification. The existing 'metadata has no home' finding covers storage schema, not who classifies the backlog.
gaps.fix: Add an explicit one-shot backfill task to Stage C: run the classifier over all open forecasts (~100 LLM calls, trivial cost), write results through the same metadata write path, and require a human spot-audit of the batch (especially direction and claim_deadline, since these can trigger immediate ~0/100 pins on old claims whose deadlines already passed). State that Stage D's shadow run is blocked on backfill completion.

gaps.title: Adversarial surface unaddressed: user-authored claim text is fed to an LLM whose output can force ~0/100 pins and deterministic glides with zero corroborating articles
gaps.argument: Forecast claims on daatan are user-authored free text, and the plan routes that text directly into an LLM classifier whose outputs (direction=survival, claim_deadline 'from claim TEXT, not resolveByDatetime', τ_lead statutory, hard-exclusion windows) directly set λ=0 or an exact ~0/100 pin 'zero articles needed'. This is a prompt-injection and crafted-phrasing surface: a user can embed instructions in claim text, or simply phrase a claim so the parser extracts an already-elapsed statutory window or a survival direction, obtaining a guaranteed near-100 AI estimate that lends the platform's credibility to their forecast and drives the 80%-crossing Telegram 'consider resolving' alert. Unlike today's article-driven estimates (which require external sources), the clock/impossibility path is the first estimate channel controlled end-to-end by a single user's input. The existing 'unaudited LLM parse' finding treats this as a data-quality error rate; nobody treats it as adversarial, and the plan has no moderation gate, no cross-check against resolveByDatetime, and no cap on how far classifier-only metadata may move an estimate.
gaps.evidence: Plan Section 2 ('claim_deadline (from claim TEXT, not resolveByDatetime — they diverge)'), Section 2 Boundaries ('pin ~0/100 exactly, zero articles needed'), Section 1 (Telegram alert on crossing 80). daatan is a reputation platform where displayed AI estimates influence user commitments.
gaps.fix: Add an adversarial-input subsection to the design doc: (a) classifier prompt hardened against instructions embedded in claim text; (b) impossibility pins require claim_deadline and resolveByDatetime to be consistent (or flag for human review when they diverge by more than a threshold); (c) classifier-only pins (no article evidence) are marked provisional in the API response and excluded from the 80%-alert trigger; (d) add a test-suite of adversarial claim texts to Stage C acceptance.

gaps.title: No failure isolation for shared fitted parameters: one bad λ₀/γ/τ fit silently moves every forecast in a topic class, with no clamps, versioning, or drift monitor
gaps.argument: λ₀ is fitted 'per topic class' and γ, τ, m₀, silence-strength are global (Section 3). These constants are multiplied into every forecast's daily glide, so a single mis-fit — e.g. λ₀ for 'geopolitics' fitted high off the longshot-biased Polymarket tranches the literature findings flag — moves the entire class of production estimates in lockstep, every day, with no news to blame and nothing that would notice. The plan's only safety device is the Stage C config flag, which is all-or-nothing: there is no per-class or per-archetype kill switch, no clamp on the maximum per-day clock-driven movement of an estimate, no bound on the clock term's share of the pooled logit, and no fleet-level monitor (e.g. 'median clock-driven daily delta per class') that would surface a poisoned parameter before users do. The plan also never versions fitted constants, so after a refit nobody can attribute an estimate change to parameters vs. evidence, or reproduce the numbers a past snapshot was computed with.
gaps.evidence: Plan Section 3 ('Parameters λ₀ (per topic class), τ, γ, m₀, silence-strength: fitted'), Section 4 Stage C ('behind a config flag' — the only rollback lever named). Confirmed findings already establish the fits will be noisy (pilot ~10 effective events, τ from one episode), which makes a bad shared parameter the expected case, not a tail risk.
gaps.fix: Add to Stage C: (1) a per-day movement clamp on the clock term (e.g. |ΔP| ≤ X pts/day absent new evidence) and a cap on its pooled weight; (2) per-topic-class enable flags so one class can be reverted without disabling the feature; (3) a parameter-set version id stored on every snapshot the clock influences; (4) a daily fleet metric (distribution of clock-driven deltas per class) with an alert threshold, defined before enablement.

gaps.title: No rollback/remediation story: flag-off stops future drift but clock-written snapshots, fired alerts, and commitments made against drifted estimates persist untagged
gaps.argument: Stage C writes clock-influenced estimates through the live pipeline into ContextSnapshot/Prediction history, the forecast page, and the ≥80% Telegram alert path. If the model is later killed (Section 3's own kill criterion contemplates exactly this) or a parameter fit proves bad, disabling the config flag only stops NEW computation: weeks of drifted snapshots remain in the user-visible timeline and in the data later used for validation ('validate on daatan's own resolved forecasts' — which would now include clock-contaminated history), alerts already fired cannot be unfired, and user commitments placed while the displayed AI estimate was wrong are permanent reputation events. Because nothing in the plan tags a snapshot as clock-driven vs article-driven, post-hoc cleanup cannot even identify which rows to exclude or annotate. The confirmed shadow-run-isolation finding covers Stage D's separate storage; this is the distinct gap for the flag-ENABLED live path, which the plan treats as reversible when it is not.
gaps.evidence: Plan Section 4 Stage C (flag is the only rollback mechanism; writes go through 'the existing logit pool'), Section 3 step 2 (future fitting/validation reads daatan's own snapshot history), Section 3 step 4 (kill criterion presumes the option to 'keep the simple one').
gaps.fix: Require every persisted estimate to carry provenance (clock term contribution, parameter version, flag state) in the snapshot record before Stage C enables in prod. Define the rollback runbook in the design doc: flag-off procedure, query to identify clock-influenced snapshots, policy for annotating (not deleting) them, and an exclusion filter so future fitting/validation never trains on clock-contaminated history. Enable on staging first, then prod behind the per-class flags.
